{"number":839,"title":"Declarative checks: review document + the implementation it recommends","body":"The #838 review document plus, at the owner's direction, all five implementation bundles it distilled. Eight commits, in dependency order:

1. **Review document** — `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md`: measured census and sweep timings, vocabulary and message analysis, per-rule conversion audit, framework survey (adopt idioms, adopt no tool).
2. **Vocabulary facilities** — `scanFileClasses`/`excludeFileClasses` (shared named file sets), structural self-exclusion of a skill's own content, rule-level `fix` default, `scanIgnoringComments` (string-aware), and full spec-key validation so a typo'd key throws instead of silently asserting nothing.
3. **jwt conversion** — the five jwt rules become two `declared-checks.json` files; the rule modules, both `checks.mjs` and the pack's `scan.mjs` are deleted (~160 net lines out), tests exercise the declared rules through the same fixtures.
4. **Perf** — the barrier scan gets a precomputed completion index + per-context shared scan state (274ms → ~180ms, findings byte-identical), and the base-ref refresh gains a 5-minute per-ref freshness window (1.21s → 0.53s back-to-back; the Stop hook no longer pays the fetch every turn).
5. **Key merges** — `checkParsedFile`/`forEachParsedEntry`/`equalParsedValues` → one select-then-assert `checkParsedFiles`; `listedInFile`/`coveredByGlobLine` → `requireIndexCoverage` with the divergent absence/anchoring semantics declared per entry. Legacy spellings stay accepted (member local packs may carry them; a rename has no fleet carrier) and normalize at load.
6. **Message discipline** — a blocking `declared-check-messages` meta-check (32-word cap per field, no fix repeated within a rule), authored red-first (17 findings), and the rewrite that turns it green. Tally recomputed 89 → 90; the stale basics row corrected.
7. **Barriers rephrase** — the scan engine moves to `engine/checks/helpers/reference-scanning.mjs`; the vocabulary gains `forbidReferences`; the three fixed barriers (claudinite-isolation, product-wiki-isolation, pack-independence) become declared checks in their owning packs, byte-identical findings on the home (minus the `doc` field declared checks drop). The per-repo config rule and the `contributes` seam keep working on the moved engine.

**Consumer safety**: two new rehearsal fixtures/changes — a member whose local pack declares checks in a legacy spelling converges green under the new blocking meta-check; the consumer-safe-change guard was satisfied by fixture (additive change), not record. At merge time, the standing verify-through-a-member rule applies: force a fleet baseline and confirm one member's converge before calling it shipped.

Verification: 1668/1668 tests, world sweep 0 blocking, work sweep clean, barrier-family findings diffed byte-identical against the pre-change baseline.

Refs #838

{"number":1569,"title":"Retire jwt-advisory-watch; keeping a pack current becomes canon curation's upstream-watch","body":"Closes #1568

A pack's `tasks/` are work every **member** repo runs, so `jwt-advisory-watch` charged the fleet for
a duty that is the canon's — and made it unrepeatable: one bespoke watcher per pack that wanted one.
The task is deleted, and the duty moves to the shelf's curator.

## How a pack declares its upstream

An optional `## Upstream` section in the pack's `README.md`, one line per source — what to watch,
where it publishes, and the state the pack's content was last reconciled against:

```md
## Upstream

- **RFC 8725 — JWT Best Current Practices** — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725
  — reconciled through RFC 8725 (BCP 225), February 2020
```

Presence of the section is the whole opt-in, and silence is a legitimate answer — most packs teach
something that does not move on anyone else's clock. The reason a source is worth watching, and what
a reconciliation concluded, stay in the pack's `references.md`.

## The task

`claudinite-canon-curation/upstream-watch` — monthly, opus, `expected_outcome: 'pr'` with
`automerge: 'nothing'`. It greps the shelf for the section, reads what each source published since
its anchor, corrects the packs that were dated by it (bumping their versions), and advances the
anchors — **only** for a source it actually read, so a refused fetch leaves its window open instead
of silently swallowing it. No signal gates it: the trigger lives outside the repo, exactly as it did
for the task it replaces. It reads the shelf and nothing else — no member repo, and no member's
dependency manifests.

A clean month is still a PR: the anchor diff is the record that the shelf was checked, and it is
what windows the next run.

## What this deliberately drops

The retired task scanned a member repo's own lockfiles for JWT libraries sitting inside an advisory's
affected range. That is dependency-update tooling, not pack content, and nothing here replaces it.

Members need no cleanup: a standing work item whose task file is gone converges to
`task:status:rejected` on its next pickup.

## Folders touched

```
packs/jwt/                          the task deleted; the manifest header, README and
                                    VERSIONS row rewritten around the new Upstream section,
                                    which carries the RFC, advisory-database and Handbook
                                    sources with their anchors

packs/claudinite-canon-curation/    the new tasks/upstream-watch/ (declaration + worker doc);
                                    the pack's stated duties widened to keeping the shelf
                                    current, and its version bumped

packs/claudinite-lifecycle/         one adoption-policy fixture re-pointed off the deleted
                                    task's vendored path onto a live one
```

{"number":311,"title":"Interactive-comment routing: three-mode prose + conversation-surface checks","body":"## Problem

When the owner gives an interactive comment, it carries one of three build-relevant intents — a correction, a feature request, or a process change — each demanding a different flow. The corpus never stated this routing, and nothing enforced that a classification was made or that the ensuing process aligned with it.

Fixes #310
Closes #314

## Change

**Prose** (`packs/basics/RULES.md`, extending the problem-first paragraph):
- Classify each owner comment — correction (repair understanding, rework what the misread touched) / feature (requirement → requirements doc → failing test → implement) / process change (durable rules in the project's **local scope**; canon promotion stays the growth lifecycle's call) — and open the reply with an explicit `Comment class:` line.
- Both build modes share the assurance-first spine: state the expectation in its durable home, watch it fail, then fix. For rules the ladder lands at prose, "see it fail" means demonstrating the corpus gap.

**Conversation surface** (engine, deliberate core change per extending.md — a new rule surface):
- The Stop hook reads its stdin JSON and forwards `transcript_path` as `--transcript`; `ctx.conversation()` lazily parses the session (`checks/lib/transcript.mjs`, shapes verified against a real transcript); `ctx.commitsWithFiles()` gives chronological per-commit file lists. CI has no transcript, so conversation rules self-gate to `[]` — the same self-supplied relevance gate skill checks use. Recorded in DESIGN.md.

**Checks** (the owner-requested check-the-work assurances — the assessment stays judgment; that it was *made*, and that the process aligned, is enforced):
- `comment-classification` (basics): the reply to the owner's **latest** comment must declare a `Comment class:` line (latest-only keeps it convergent — a transcript is append-only).
- `feature-requirements-first` (executable-requirements): after a feature-classified comment, an independent commit updating `dev/requirements/requirements.md` (no code alongside) must precede the first code commit, scoped by the comment's timestamp so earlier branch work is never re-litigated.

## Verification

- Red-first fixtures beside each pack (`packs/basics/pack.test.mjs`, `packs/executable-requirements/pack.test.mjs`) — both suites seen failing before the implementation existed, green after; full suite 274/274.
- Live see-it-fail: run against this session's own transcript truncated to turn 1 (before the rule existed), `comment-classification` fires on exactly the omission the owner described; on the current transcript it's clean.
- Full sweep (`node checks/run.mjs`) exits clean.","state":"closed","draft":false,"merged":true,"mergeable_state":"unknown","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/311","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"merged_by":"missingbulb","head":{"ref":"claude/interactive-workflow-guidelines-ch6oki","sha":"79e0b0a047843377a7260ea325a3994dd9200920","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"679ee978bdbccc2c76999a1ee1d1015b4b841111","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"additions":449,"deletions":11,"changed_files":14,"commits":3,"created_at":"2026-07-17T05:55:35Z","updated_at":"2026-07-17T17:26:57Z","closed_at":"2026-07-17T17:26:56Z","merged_at":"2026-07-17T17:26:56Z"}

{"number":338,"title":"feature-requirements-first: resolve the spec path, self-skip when absent","body":"## Why

`feature-requirements-first` is a **check-the-work** rule, but it hardcoded the spec at `dev/requirements/requirements.md`. A project whose executable spec lives elsewhere — a non-canonical layout, or the pack pulled in via `spec-driven-product`'s `requires` without the canonical file — got a finding **no correct work could clear**: you can't land a doc-first commit to a spec file that isn't yours and doesn't exist.

That's the anti-pattern: the only escapes were the wrong instruments — an `accept` (a check-the-**world** mechanism, permanent, that a *successive run wouldn't even re-find* since the rule is scoped to this session's feature turn + this branch's pending commits) or a post-hoc rebase. It surfaced landing a feature in CrosswordChat (spec at `dev/docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`), where an `accept` was the only way through — which was itself the wrong tool.

## The principle

A check-the-work rule must **always be satisfiable by doing the work right, or not fire at all**. This change makes `feature-requirements-first` obey that:

1. **Resolve the spec path from the project** — `config.spec` on the `executable-requirements` pack entry, defaulting to the canonical `dev/requirements/requirements.md`. A non-canonical project declares its spec once and gets ordering enforcement against its *real* spec.
2. **Self-skip when the resolved spec is absent** from the repo, instead of emitting a finding no commit could clear.

## Changes

- `packs/executable-requirements/feature-requirements-first.mjs` — `specPath(ctx)` resolves `config.spec` → canonical default; `run()` self-skips when `!ctx.exists(spec)` and enforces ordering against the resolved path.
- `packs/executable-requirements/pack.test.mjs` — three red-first tests: self-skip when the spec is absent; honor a configured non-canonical path (doc-first passes); with a configured path, code-before-spec still fires.

Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

{"number":128,"title":"Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement","body":"## What this is

Reorganizes the corpus from always/soft-loaded instructions into **two homes selected by *when* a rule is active**, plus a deterministic enforcement engine:

- **`packs/<name>/`** — a bundle of prose (`RULES.md`) *and* checks, active **once per session** by the project's `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration (`universal` always on). Active packs' prose is injected by a SessionStart hook; their checks run at every Stop and in CI. A dependency-free registry discovers packs by directory scan — no list to maintain.
- **`skills/<name>/`** — activity-scoped procedures the harness surfaces on demand; content inlined in each `SKILL.md` (no cross-tree redirect).
- **`checks/`** — the engine only: the runner, lib, the Stop hook, the PreToolUse guard, and their red-first fixtures.

`always/`, `tasks/`, `technologies/`, and `templates/` are gone — folded into the two homes.

## The model (design in `checks/DESIGN.md`)

- **Promotion ladder**: platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose. A rule lives in the cheapest mechanism that can carry it; prose is the audited fallback.
- **Checks** are declared+closed (every rule of a declared pack runs every time), drift-guarded by a structural fingerprint meta-check; diff-scoped only as a transitional aid (whole-repo sweep is the default); reasoned acceptances; fail-fast severity (advisory is a per-rule *kind*, not a burn-in stage).
- **Platform settings are verified, never trusted** — an offline effect check (squash-only ⇒ no merge commits in main's first-parent history) plus a config check later.
- **Technology gotchas convert per-gotcha** by whether they have a static artifact signature; the rest is pack prose.
- **Skills**: model-invoked routing is probabilistic, so nothing that *must* happen rides on a skill — enforcement is checks/hooks/settings. (Skill-scoped hooks exist, verified, for the rare activity-scoped enforcement need.)
- **Growth is checks-first**: promote descends the ladder for each new lesson; a `prose-to-checks` skill sweeps the existing prose backlog for always-testable rules the conversion missed.

## Implemented (all green: 42 tests, CI passing, sweep clean)

- Runner + registry; **universal pack** (7 checks) + **github-actions** (6) + **chrome-extension** conformance (6); the pack-prose SessionStart loader; the Stop hook and PreToolUse guard.
- Full pack prose (baseline, technology packs, the chrome-extension release standard, the research-project class pack); 12 inlined skills (command + practice) + the prose-to-checks skill.
- Bootstrap Parts 6–7 (hooks, `--init`, skill symlinks); index, README, DESIGN, growth docs all updated to the two-home model.

## The checks earned their keep repeatedly

They caught real defects at every stage — dangling links and a label/href mismatch on `main`; **nine historical merge commits** that had bypassed the squash-only policy unnoticed (now sha-keyed acceptances); real pipefail defects in the canon release workflows; and several of my own regressions mid-restructure (the Stop hook blocked me in-session more than once).

**Owner action outstanding:** flip the squash-only merge *setting* (repo Settings → General) — unreachable from here; the effect check covers the gap meanwhile.

Closes #127
Closes #131

{"number":541,"title":"Growth promote: 10 lessons from 7 members into the canon","body":"Run of 2026-07-29. Read the local packs of 7 members, generalized the portable lessons, deduped each against the whole corpus. Refs #537.

**No auto-merge armed** — this is the judgment gate before shared canon; owner approves.

## Promoted

| # | Origin | Landed | Generalized rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EdFringeNow | `basics` / engineering-practices (sharpens the existing `git ls-files` bullet) | A `git ls-files`-derived sweep sees only *tracked* files, so a brand-new file sits outside it until committed — the run's "checked N files" line is not evidence your new file was among them. |
| 2 | CrosswordChat | `basics` / engineering-practices | A capability applied best-effort behind a *silent* fallback must record whether it actually engaged; otherwise every later measurement of it is uninterpretable. |
| 3 | LaughCounter | `basics` / engineering-practices | Everything the software persists on a user's machine lives under one user-deletable location; a new need extends it rather than earning a second one. |
| 4 | LaughCounter | `basics` / engineering-practices | A user-facing data disclosure (permission usage string, privacy policy, store listing) is part of the behaviour's contract — it changes in the same commit; adding retention/egress/a listener is a change to the promise, not a new field. |
| 5 | EdFringeNow | `basics` / engineering-practices | When a session drives an external runtime more than once, write one argv-parameterised driver into the scratchpad and re-point it, rather than a fresh throwaway per invocation. |
| 6 | GoogleCalendarEventCreator | `git-github` / git-github-advanced (new section) | Cap **and** qualify every list/search call — an unqualified query is a full-text search returning full bodies, and an unpaged one blows the tool-result cap; both bounds are needed, not either. |
| 7 | ShoutsAndWhispers | `basics` / writing-tests | A format implemented twice (two languages/tiers) is held together only by a shared vector set carried deliberately by *both* suites — a vector asserted on one side is an input nobody compared; touching either implementation re-runs both. |
| 8 | VascularColoring | `research-project` §5 (new subsection) | A metric's definition is part of its identity: re-defining one is the owner's call, and the recorded history is re-measured, never re-labelled — the column keeps its name while the quantity moves. |
| 9 | VascularColoring | `research-project` §1 | State each reported number's trust boundary inline beside it, not in a separate caveats section. |
| 10 | EdFringeNow | `node` (new "Module resolution" section) | A named import off a package's CJS entry can silently resolve to `undefined` — import the ESM entry for named bindings; and modern Node (22.7+) detects ES-module syntax in `.js`, so a directory of ES modules needs no `package.json` to declare it. |

**All ten landed as prose**, each for the same reason: they are in-flight judgment or runtime/tool behaviour with no repo-state signature a check could read (no grounded case has a file-scoped shape to match). No conformance-backlog issue is warranted.

Catalog upkeep in the same change: `packs/node/README.md` rule rows, and the `node` / `research-project` prose counts in `packs/README.md`.

## Notable rejections

- **CrosswordChat / browser-speech** — essentially the whole pack is already covered by the canon `web-speech` pack (recognizer owns its capture, constrained-then-bare preflight retry, pause watchdog with the 1.2 s/1.8 s window, on-device biasing gate, lazy `getVoices()`, error taxonomy, `chrome.tts` relay). Only the silent-fallback instrumentation point (#2) was genuinely new.
- **gRatio** — fully covered by the canon `research-project` pack (no single-input special-casing, prior-free/scale-free rules, "name the hard constraint", numbered notes with the rejected list, validation tiers, cross-domain out-of-band). Nothing to promote.
- **ShoutsAndWhispers — "a geohash bounds query is a candidate query, post-filter by true distance"**: portable, but it restates well-documented upstream `geofire` behaviour, and the canon homes no geospatial technology. Minting a stub pack from a single member's usage is the wrong instrument — flagging it for `growth-discover-packs` instead.
- **EdFringeNow — the Playwright launch recipe** (no `executablePath`; the browsers path is already exported by the environment): real and repeatedly costly, but Playwright has no pack home. The transferable halves are promoted as #5 and #10; the Playwright-specific residue is likewise left for `growth-discover-packs`.
- Several member rules turned out to be canon already and were left untouched: `pkill -f` self-match, `git checkout <ref> -- <paths>`, cross-file shared constants / drift guards, GENERATED-file discipline, "the vendored canon reflects its stamp, not upstream `main`".

## Coverage gap in this run

`missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite` was named in the dispatching context but was **outside this session's repo access**, so its local packs could not be read. Worth a follow-up run once that repo is in scope.

{"number":372,"title":"node: earn-each-dependency check (prose-to-checks: engineering-practices "Earn each dependency")","body":"Weekly **prose-to-checks** sweep (`skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md`). Converts the always-testable slice of one existing prose rule. Closes the loop on a conversion `docs/conversion-inventory.md` already planned. Refs #371.

## The rule

`skills/engineering-practices/SKILL.md`: *"Earn each dependency: prefer a built-in (or a few lines) for a narrow job, and drop one when the assumption that justified it lapses."*

Only the **event** — a `package.json` gains a dependency it did not carry before — has a static signature. That converts; the judgment half stays prose.

## The check — `node/earn-each-dependency` (advisory)

- **Home:** the `node` pack (its first check). `package.json` is a node artifact, so relevance is gated by the pack's declaration per `checks/DESIGN.md`'s litmus — not fired on non-node repos.
- **Detection:** for each `package.json` at the repo root or one directory down (the node marker's own scope), diff dependency **names** across the four dependency groups between the scoping base (`ctx.readBase`) and head. A name at head but in no group at base → one advisory finding.
- **Converges (check-the-work):** fires once, on the branch that adds the dependency; once on `main`, base == head and the name is no longer new. A **version bump** and a **move between groups** (dev → prod) are not additions.

## Bounded surface

- `packs/node/earn-each-dependency.mjs` — the rule module.
- `packs/node/pack.mjs` — one-line registration (`rules: [earnEachDependency]`) + a comment refresh.
- `packs/node/pack.test.mjs` — new; six fixtures (flags an add, flags one dir down, ignores a version bump, ignores a dev→prod move, silent when unchanged, ignores a deep/fixture manifest). Red-first verified: neutering the rule reddens exactly the two flagging fixtures.

The engineering-practices prose is **left intact** — it is the rule's rationale/judgment, which the failure message references (`doc:`) rather than replaces (nothing enforcement-shaped there to trim).

## Verification

- `node --test` full suite: **508/508 green**.
- `node checks/run.mjs`: **clean (exit 0)**.

{"number":675,"title":"Three-responsibility task machinery: janitor split, precondition-only gating, prework rename, exec-status distillation","body":"Implements owner requirements 16–17 (2026-08-06), which deliberately override parts of the existing per-project-scheduling and task-prework designs. The overrides are recorded as per-project-scheduling DESIGN §12.

## What broke, explicitly

- **§5's "scheduler's maintenance pass" is retired.** `maintainDispatchIssues` left `run.mjs`; the scheduler now only creates task issues. Recovery (stale escalation, dead-claim reclaim, lost-event re-arm) plus a health review moved to a new daily `basics/task-janitor` task (`agent_model: none`, hard-coded worker over `dispatch.mjs`'s unchanged pure rules). **Stated trade:** recovery latency for a lost label event or dead claim grows from ~1h to up to a day.
- **§4's invalid-dispatch lifecycle splits.** A well-formed dispatch naming a task the repo no longer carries (file removed, pack undeclared) is now **closed** by the executor (`resolve-dispatch` exit 14, `task-gone`) — no `needs-human`, no lingering tracking issue in a failed state. Malformed/forged dispatches keep the needs-human convergence.
- **wiki-growth's documented task.md preflight is deleted** (it was a knowing exception): the open-growth-PR gate moved into its precondition, enabled by the `prs` signal now carrying open-PR labels. The per-run "dated nudge comment" on the waiting PR is gone with it.
- **The "pre-agent preprocessing" framing is gone.** Execution is two similar, consecutive phases: **prework**, then **agentic work**. Contract fields `prework` / `prework_timeout` (legacy `agent_preprocessing*` accepted and normalized at load; the shape check flags them; migration note drives member local-pack renames). `docs/agent-preprocessing/` → `docs/task-prework/`; run-record outcome `preprocess` → `prework` (parser reads both).

## New mechanisms

- **`task-phase-discipline`** (basics, advisory world check): hunts tasks that "escape" after their precondition passed — conditional-skip language in task.md, cycle-skip strings in prework workers. Heuristics taken from the real violations found in the audit; precondition-describing and Context-scoped lines are exempt.
- **Exec-status distillation from conversation logs, fully hard-coded:** executor terminal states print `claudinite-task-exec v1 <pack>/<task> [<slot>] <status>` (`success`/`failed` via new `record-exec.mjs`; `task-gone`/`invalid` printed by `resolve-dispatch` itself; format owned by `run-record.mjs`). The captured executor transcripts carry them to the logs branch, and `usage-fold` counts them into new `taskExec` rows beside the scheduler-side census (invocations, precondition passes, prework runs, failures, deferrals). skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.3 records this.
- **Doctrine:** scheduled-tasks.md now states the three-responsibility split and the precondition-is-the-only-decision-point rule (failures may stop a run; discretion may not; empty outcome is always legal; the conditional agent hand-off may escalate only on work prework could not do).

## Rule-17 audit of all 17 canon/local tasks

- **Violated:** wiki-growth (fixed here — gate moved to precondition).
- **Borderline:** baselining (worker declines to deliver a completed converge while a prior PR stands; also re-states its precondition's stamp test) — left in place but now flagged by the new check; its kept-PR path's return-shape **crash bug** is fixed here. Minor: tidy-issues ("already ⇒ skip" in a one-line idempotent sub-step), growth-extract (agent re-derives `retention_days` the precondition already decided).
- **Adhere:** the other 13. `CLAUDINITE_REQUEST_AGENT` is used once (baselining) and its four gates are genuine judgment-left conditions.

## Considered and declined

URL-invoked executor routines instead of label events: the label is both trigger and write-gated authorization, the re-arm recovery is built on it, and a URL endpoint would add a callable credential per repo. Recorded in DESIGN §12.6.

- Full unit suite: 1234 pass, 0 fail.

## 2026-08-08 · born · Add the jwt pack, distilled from The JWT Handbook (#705)
- **Source:** The JWT Handbook (Sebastián E. Peyrott, Auth0, v0.14.2): chapters 2-6 for
  applications and JWS/JWE/JWK structure, Annex A for the pitfalls, attacks and best current
  practices.
- **Reason:** token budget was the design constraint, so the pack injects no session-start prose at
  all and the book's teaching lands in deterministic-first layers instead: five checks whose failure
  message is the rule, and two action skills read only at usage time for what a static sweep cannot
  judge. Scoped to generic JWT practice, leaving the Google-issuer validator's own config and
  browser-client OAuth token acquisition to the packs that own them.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
- **Mechanism:** the pack manifest, fingerprinted by a JWT library reference (`jsonwebtoken`,
  `jose`, PyJWT and their kin) in JS/TS/Python source. The marker only suspects the pack; declaring
  it stays the project's call.
- **Rejected:** a migration record to carry members across the three new blocking checks. The pack
  is opt-in, a fingerprint only suspects and baselining never auto-declares, so no existing member
  could turn red; a rehearsal fixture proving a member that does opt in converges green was the
  additive answer, negative-probed by hand against a hardcoded secret and an unpinned verify.
- **Landed:** #705 (Closes #706) · pack version 1.

## 2026-09-01 · moved · the pack's advisory watch becomes canon curation's upstream-watch (#1569)

  per pack that wanted one. Deliberately dropped with it: scanning a member's own lockfiles for JWT
  libraries inside an advisory's affected range, which is dependency-update tooling rather than pack
  content, and nothing replaces it.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude, per the commit trailer.
- **Mechanism:** the README's `## Upstream` section, one line per source naming what to watch, where
  it publishes and the state this pack's content was last reconciled against; presence of the
  section is the whole opt-in, and the canon's own monthly task reads it. The pack now declares
  three sources: RFC 8725, the GitHub Advisory Database's JWT libraries for the classes of flaw the
  skills teach against, and the Handbook itself.

{"number":751,"title":"growth-promote: dedupe PR #740's rule additions and cut the language","body":"Reviewed rebuild of #740. Every rule addition there was checked for necessity against **current** `main`, the duplicates dropped, and the surviving prose rewritten terse.

Two things forced a rebuild rather than a patch on top of #740's branch:

1. **Its own dedupe was incomplete.** Merging seven branches and keeping "the longest phrasing" left several lessons standing two and three times, and one merge artifact was syntactically broken.
2. **Its base is 40 commits behind `main`.** #740's diff targets a `packs/basics/RULES.md` that still had the engineering-practices bullets in a separate skill file, and an `adopt-pack` whose catalog premise `main` has since invalidated.

## Dropped as duplicate (6)

| Lesson | What #740 did |
|---|---|
| "Not statically checkable" expires | added **3×** to `prose-to-checks` |
| Product-statement counterfactual | added **2×** to `prose-to-checks`, back to back |
| Serialized round-trip comparison | added **2×** to `writing-tests` |
| A skip still exits 0 / self-updating mechanism | added **2× each** to `unattended-agents` |
| Human-only step gets its own issue | added to **both** `basics/RULES.md` and `git-github-advanced` |
| Sibling-repo copy is a canon candidate | added to **both** `basics/RULES.md` and `extracting-lessons.md` |

Also dropped: `unattended-agents`' cap-and-qualify bullet (already canon in `git-github-advanced`, "Cap *and* qualify every list/search call"), and its restatements of the tool-search and summarizing-fetch contracts that now sit once in `basics/RULES.md`.

`prose-to-checks`' severity list was left broken by the merge — item 3 read `directional by kind, or when …` followed by a stray `directional by kind.` from the other side. Repaired.

## Dropped as obsolete (1)

`adopt-pack`'s "the mount holds only what it already adopted, so shallow-clone the canon to enumerate the catalog" is **false on current main**: `compute-vendor-set` ships `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` with every mount, declared packs or none (asserted by `compute-vendor-set.test.mjs:148`). Only the match-the-owner's-plain-words-to-a-pack-id half survives, as one sentence on the existing catalog paragraph.

## Re-homed (2)

#661 folded `skills/engineering-practices/SKILL.md` into `packs/basics/RULES.md`. #740 still edits the deleted file — the landmine its own description flagged. The unknown-state rule and the widened self-description bullet land in `RULES.md` instead.

## Kept, terser

`basics/RULES.md` (dispatch-prompt classification, shared-pack-before-hand-authoring, three harness-tool contracts, text-finding waivers, blocked-host policy boundary, human-only-step issue, unknown-state, multi-site disclosure claims) · `authoring-agent-docs` (withdrawn practices rewritten present-tense) · `writing-tests` (serialized round-trip) · `git-github-advanced` (auto-merge refusals, `.gitignore` pruning trap, green-run-≠-job-ran) · `extracting-lessons` (two kinds that never become a pack rule) · `prose-to-checks` (counterfactual, "already covered" is a claim to test, expiring un-checkability, irreversible-condition severity, positive allowlist, form-not-intent) · `unattended-agents` (skip-in-a-green-run, fresh-context judgment stages, re-issuing rejected guard calls, unedittable tracker posts) · `node` (`node --test` skips dot-directories) · `research-project` (per-input calibration, figure-only methods, explicit gap lists).

## Verification

- `node --test` over `packs-tests/`, `engine-tests/`, `vendoring/`, `dev/` — **1347 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking, 17 advisory**; verified identical on a stashed tree, so this change adds none.

Refs #740

{"number":853,"title":"Promote eleven fleet lessons into the canon","body":"Growth promote, 2026-08-15. Context members read: **ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog** — their local packs' `RULES.md` prose and check modules.

Eleven lessons cleared the bar. Six are folds into an existing rule (a measured sharpening of what the corpus already said); five are new bullets in a doc that owns the subject. Every one is prose — the reasons are per-row below. `Refs #852`.

**Rebased onto current `main`** (24 commits, including the `basics/RULES.md` audit in #894) and re-applied in the style that audit landed — see *Conformance to the audited style* below.

| Lesson (generalized) | Origin | Landed |
|---|---|---|
| Naming a path in `node --test` is not enough — the argument must resolve to files that exist; a typo'd glob is the same zero-test green | ClaudiniteWebsite (`node-test-discovery` check) | `packs/node/RULES.md` — sharpens the test-discovery bullet |
| When you know the exact title, don't search — an MCP layer may match *semantically* and honour no qualifier, so `in:title` filters nothing; enumerate and match in-session | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — sharpens "Cap *and* qualify" |
| The per-object **field set** is the payload knob, not the page size — the same call at two page sizes returned identical output | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — same section, new sub-bullet |
| A rebase that drops part of a branch must amend the commit message in the same step — under squash merge the commit body *is* `main`'s record, and a PR comment isn't carried | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — commit-layering section |
| Find an already-open issue by the **invariant identifier** the finding names, never the sentence it arrived in — every filer paraphrases the message | MissingBulbWebsite | `packs/basics/RULES.md` — folded into the "Deferring a warning" rule |
| A harness wake-up needs `prompt` unless `stop: true`; a no-op flag and a `reason` don't exempt it | ClaudiniteWebsite + Sheepdog + MissingBulbWebsite (3 of 4) | `packs/basics/RULES.md` — Harness-tool contracts |
| Telling a reader to *run* something ships the literal invocation, not the filename (measured 5/5 vs 0/5 first-try) — and a rule filed where its reader never looks cannot repair a defective instruction | Sheepdog | `authoring-agent-docs` — "Shape a rule so it fires" + "Maintain it like code" |
| Seeing a figure in several search results is not evidence of who published it — snippets quote each other; attribute to the named origin | MissingBulbWebsite | `packs/product-wiki/RULES.md` |
| A dedupe search that finds nothing, on a rule naming an identifier you don't own, more likely means the mechanism **expired** than that the lesson is novel | Sheepdog | `extracting-lessons.md` — extends "Dedupe ruthlessly" |
| A test dereferencing a path in a read-only dependency tree someone else refreshes is a test whose fixture a stranger can delete — read defensively, skip with a stated reason | Sheepdog | `writing-tests` |
| An open PR is invisible to the next pass reading only the default branch — read open PRs on the same paths, not just the tracker log | MissingBulbWebsite | `unattended-agents` — extends the tracker-log precondition |

### Conformance to the audited style

Three of these were re-applied differently after the rebase, because #894 changed what the corpus asks for:

- **The issue-search rule is now a clause, not a bullet.** Its subject was "Looking for *that* already-open issue" — a "that" pointing back, which the audited skill names as the test for a rule that is a clause of its neighbour. It folds into "Deferring a warning" instead.
- **The run-it-don't-name-it rule drops its incident narrative.** "Carrying the evidence a rule came from" now says the story and the ids are archaeology the commit keeps, and only a measurement that *is* the argument stays — so the 0-in-5 / 5-in-5 figure survives and the run-by-run account doesn't.
- **The dedupe-miss rule sheds its closing clause**, which #894's own "cut the one whose mechanism has since been retired" now carries. What remains is the half that audit doesn't make: that an *empty* dedupe search reads as novelty when it more often means expiry.

Two smaller ones: the `git-github-advanced` addition gets the blank line between blocks the style now asks for (the pre-existing unseparated run below it is left alone), and the `node/RULES.md` bullet this extends is **wrapped at 100 columns** per `rules-line-length`'s own remedy — that file goes from 6 over-long lines to 5, and its other five are untouched.

**One sentence added that no source had**, which the style rule requires be named as an addition: "Naming a mechanism" now points at its exception ("The exception is a mechanism you are telling the reader to *run*, below"), so the general rule doesn't read as unconditional.

Still-needed check: none of the eleven is covered by anything in the 24 commits `main` gained. The nearest miss is the dedupe-miss rule above, trimmed rather than dropped.

### Why prose, not checks

Ten of the eleven are **judgment or in-flight behaviour** with no repo-state signature (how to phrase an instruction, which tool to reach for, what a search miss means). The one convertible item is the `node --test` sharpening: ClaudiniteWebsite already runs it as a working check with a fixture. It is not lifted here because the lesson was **already canon prose** — this is a fold-in to an existing rule, and converting canon prose to a canon check is the standing `prose-to-checks` sweep's own territory, which reads `packs/node/RULES.md` and will now see the sharpened property to assert. Flagged in the tracker rather than minted as a backlog issue.

### Notable rejections (already covered)

- Dispatch-prompt `Comment class:` (3 members) — `basics` already carries "Replying to an automation dispatch prompt".
- `select:` needs the `mcp__<server>__` prefix; `Edit` needs the read tool — both already in `basics` Harness-tool contracts.
- "The session that designed a judgment stage must not run it"; "re-issue a rejected fallback"; "nothing you post to a tracker can be edited" — all already in `unattended-agents` (the wake-up bullet above carries only the argument contract and points at that rule rather than restating it).
- "Grep the standing absolutes when a change falsifies a self-description" — already in `basics`.
- "A step only the owner can perform gets its own issue"; "look for the shared pack before hand-authoring release/CI plumbing" — both already in `basics`.
- ClaudiniteWebsite's "shallow-clone the canon to list adoptable packs" — **expired**, superseded by `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` shipping in every mount; `core` already routes there.
- Sheepdog's `resolve-dispatch` exit-11 echo — a fix to `engine/scheduler/executor.md`, outside promote's `packs/`+`skills/` write surface.

### Verification (re-run after the rebase)

- `check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking, 60 advisory**, identical to `origin/main`'s own 60; no advisory introduced.
- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1836 pass, 0 fail**.
- `promote-scope.mjs` — OK, every changed path under `packs/`.
- Diff against `main` removes 5 lines, all of them the tails of rules this PR extends; no other author's content is touched.

{"number":524,"title":"Skill-usage metrics: enriched capture, per-repo fold, fleet aggregation","body":"Closes #520. Implements `docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md` in full — all three stages, all deterministic code, no agent judgment anywhere in the pipeline.

## 1. Capture enrichment (`grow_with_claudinite`)

- **`--issue 0` is legal**, meaning "no associated issue". The filename *shape* stays byte-identical on purpose: the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename parse all already accept `0`, whereas a new shape would be invisible to the prune and become immortal on the branch. `conversation-extract`'s task.md now states that an `issue-0` log has no issue to post its exchange summary on.
- **A SessionEnd hook** (`engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs`), registered like its siblings via `REQUIRED_HOOKS` + bootstrap Part 5. It picks up the sessions that never merge (a review, an investigation) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that do. Best-effort and fail-soft: every error is swallowed and logged, and it can never block a session from ending.
- **The delta contract is now pinned by tests** — repeat capture of an unchanged transcript produces nothing (no file, no commit), and a post-merge `--issue 0` capture holds exactly the tail. Double-writing is safe *by construction*, not by coordination, and that is a property of capture rather than of the hook, so it is tested where it lives.

### One deviation from the design, stated

DESIGN §3.3 has the hook itself run capture. The canon's `barriers` config forbids `engine/**` from naming any pack (`core must not name the specific packs it runs`), and the hook is engine-side because hook registration is. So the engine file is a **runner**: it invokes each active pack's own `session-end.mjs`, discovered structurally exactly as tasks, prose and skills are. `grow_with_claudinite/session-end.mjs` is the step that captures with `--issue 0`. Same final behaviour, no barrier exception, and it matches DESIGN §1's own placement table (capture lives in the pack) more closely than putting the invocation in core would.

## 2. `usage-fold` (per repo, daily, agentless, `merged-pr`)

Counts skill loads **and the denominators** (`captures`, `merges`, `sessions`, `userMessages`, `userCommands`) out of the logs the pack already captures, into `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` — day rows recomputed statelessly inside the raw window, week rows appended once past a `foldedThrough` watermark.

Every entry shape the counting classifies was **verified against real captured transcripts** on a `conversation-logs` branch, not inferred. Notably, `userMessages` tests **for** the human marker (`origin.kind === 'human'`) rather than against a list of automated ones — so a scheduled-task firing, a task notification, a compaction summary, a slash-command expansion and a subagent turn are all excluded, and a *new* automated shape is excluded the day it appears instead of silently inflating the denominator. That heuristic is one function with a fixture per shape it excludes.

The fold ran over this repo's real logs branch during development and produced plausible numbers (e.g. `2026-W30`: 16 captures, 14 session-days, 87 user messages, `merge-to-main` 6 loads).

## 3. `fleet-usage` (sheepdog, daily, agentless, `merged-pr`)

A **stateless full recompute** over the members' own usage files into `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` in the enforcer repo. Members are enumerated at runtime from the sheepdog config via `fleet-api.mjs`, exactly as the census does — **no repo is named in canon anywhere**. Full week × repo × skill grain, nothing pre-summed, so every coarser view stays derivable. Missing or unreadable member files are listed in `coverage.absent` **with the reason**, never skipped silently, and a `_note` states the sampling population so the file cannot be read as a census.

## The shared delivery primitive

Both aggregate writes ride an auto-merging PR through one new engine module, `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs`. It commits via **git plumbing** (throwaway index seeded from the fetched base tip) rather than checking a branch out: the scheduler runs every due task in **one checkout**, so a task that checked a branch out would hand the next task a tree it did not expect, and an auto-merging PR could carry another task's commits along with it. The test drives it against a dirty checkout sitting on someone else's branch and asserts HEAD, the index and the working tree all come back untouched.

That test caught a real bug on its first run: `execFileSync` with an explicit `stdio: ['ignore', …]` and an `input` silently feeds the child nothing, so `hash-object --stdin` cheerfully wrote the **empty blob** — a wrong answer, not an error.

## Also

- `bundledSkillSources` extracted into the pack registry, so "which skills does this repo mount" has one definition shared by the SessionStart mount hook and the fold (the fold must never read `.claude/skills/`, which is gitignored session state an Action checkout has no copy of).
- The fold declares its own `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` entry, so the GENERATED file the canon's own discipline governs arrives already conforming instead of tripping `generated-merge-driver` fleet-wide.

## Verification

- `605/605` tests pass (`+30` new across capture idempotence, the hook runner, the counting core, the fold worker's drift guards, the fleet aggregation, and the delivery plumbing).
- `check_the_world`: 0 blocking (8 advisories, all pre-existing `file-placement` distance notes matching their siblings). `check_the_work`: clean.
- Drift guards added where two files must agree without importing each other: the fold's filename parse against `capture-log.mjs`'s writer, and the sweep's member path against the fold's write path — a rename on either side would otherwise produce a plausible, entirely wrong "the whole fleet reports zero".

## Rollout

No migration record, per DESIGN §7: the nightly vendored-canon refresh carries the code and `converge-wiring`'s `REQUIRED_HOOKS` registers the hook, both already run by baselining. The one ordering constraint — idempotence + `issue-0` landing before the hook fires anywhere — is satisfied by all of §3 shipping in this one PR.

{"number":1671,"title":"Promote the reviewed survivors of nine growth-promote PRs","body":"Consolidates #1021, #1157, #1204, #1345, #1372, #1409, #1451, #1524 and #1661 (all closed in favour of this one) into one reviewed change, then re-reviewed against `main` after #1711. Each candidate was judged against the corpus; what stays is one copy each of the rules that add something `main` does not already carry, written to the `writing-pack-prose` ration, and every rule with a signature the four-moment vocabulary can carry rides a check instead of prose.

**Converted to checks** (each with a fixture that failed before its declaration existed; the prose each covers is deleted whole)

- `packs/basics` action guards — `ask-user-question-already-decided` (advisory context on every `AskUserQuestion`), `bare-wait-in-fresh-shell` (blocking, `since` today: a `wait` in a Bash call that launched nothing), `manufactured-no-op-call` (advisory: `sleep 1; echo waiting`, `true`).
- `packs/git-github` action guards — `issue-labels-overwrite` (advisory), `pull-request-head-unqualified` (blocking, `since` today), `codeload-tarball-fetch` (blocking, `since` today), `search-code-lower-bound` (advisory).
- `packs/node` world check — `node/btoa-atob-on-text` (advisory, comment-stripped).
- Also from the source PRs: `no-conflict-markers` (blocking) and `comment-classification-form` (advisory work rule), and `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` widened to `workflow_run`/`repository_dispatch`.

**Kept as prose**

- `packs/basics` — retiring a system into another; polling with an `until` loop (the half the wait guard can't see); pasteable command blocks without trailing `#`; doc claims a behavior change falsifies; the `ToolSearch` rule's fully-enumerated-roster exception. - `packs/git-github` — `git-github-advanced`: write scope is a policy boundary (moved here from basics, beside its subject), amend-not-`filter-branch`, curl reading an error body as zero pending, one wait mechanism, unreachable artifact URLs, generated-file races with a scheduled writer, `list_pull_requests`' `merged` field, `issue_read` on a PR number, subscribing every PR a sweep leaves open, `actions_list` ignoring `per_page`.
- `packs/claudinite-growth` — `unattended-agents`: sharpened shared-checkout rule plus three subagent-dispatch lessons; `extract-from-conversations`: a captured JSONL line can overflow a raw `Read`.
- `packs/claudinite-lifecycle` — the badge row after a declaration change, vendor-set evidence, running the world sweep locally.
- `packs/ios` (first two rules), `packs/node` (scratchpad scripts, the CI Node pin), `packs/flutter` (`tester.runAsync`), `packs/research-project` (never validate against prior output).

**Dropped** — every near-duplicate framing; the public-claim rule; the `node/node-test-discovery` check (fires blocking on a bare `node --test`); the `claudinite-tasks` REST rule (retired queue model); the web-speech echo rule and the skipped-job rule (both landed on `main` since); narrow one-offs. {"number":1828,"title":"Promote the validated survivors of four growth-promote PRs","body":"Refs #1715, #1690, #1419, #1303 — all four closed as folded in.

Re-derived against current `main` rather than rebased. All four branches conflicted only on version-bump bookkeeping their own pack rules say a promotion should not write (`claudinite-growth`: *a shared canon pack's version and its `VERSIONS.md` row are the canon's own tasks' to write*), so the conflicts were dropped, not resolved.

## 27 candidates in, 9 landed

**9 were already in `main`** — mostly as checks the prose-to-checks lane landed after these branches were written:

| Candidate | Already covered by |
|---|---|
| `fields` vs `per_page` on list calls | `basics/github-list-without-fields` |
| `codeload` tarball 403 | `git-github/codeload-tarball-fetch` (blocking) |
| `btoa`/`atob` on text | `node/btoa-atob-on-text` |
| `labels` full-replace | `git-github/issue-labels-overwrite` |
| bare `head` filter | `git-github/pull-request-head-unqualified` (blocking) |
| bisection-midpoint vectors | `basics/writing-tests` SKILL |
| module resolution from the script's dir | `node/RULES.md` — and main's is stronger, naming `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and that `NODE_PATH` doesn't help |
| D1 expand/migrate/contract | `cloudflare-workers` (merged #1780) |
| Wrangler *missing* vs *unknown* | `cloudflare-workers` (merged #1780) |

Worth recording how three of those were nearly missed: grepping for each PR's **own wording** returned ABSENT for the `head` filter, module resolution and the labels trap. The `head` one only surfaced because the live check fired on my probe. Dedup has to be by subject, against the destination file — not by the candidate's phrasing.

**9 landed, each probed in this session:**

| Rule | Pack | Probe |
|---|---|---|
| Taking over a retiring repo's role | basics | working-discipline rule, no external claim |
| A blocked primary source about a real person | basics | same |
| Shared constants: pair by name across languages | basics | extends the existing rule; design guidance |
| Check the invocation line, not a display label | canon-curation | reproduced — a token grep answers 1 while the command runs 0 times |
| An engine comment citing a design doc dangles in members | lifecycle | read from `compute-vendor-set.mjs`: engine walk is a copy minus `*.md`, `DOCS_DIR` excluded |
| A silent check run is the clean result | lifecycle | `check_the_work.mjs` on a clean tree → 0 bytes, exit 0 |
| Stop re-searching for a PR template once known absent | git-github-advanced | this repo carries none |
| `task-worker-restores-main` check + test | claudinite-growth | 6 tests pass; silent on the real tree; 16 workers in scope |
| `test-discovery-resolves` check + tests | node | 14 tests pass; silent; `ci.yml` in scope |

Both checks are stamped `since: 2026-09-06` so their two-week advisory grace runs from when they actually reach members, not from their branches' dates (#1303's was written 2026-08-23 and carried none at all).

The node test file is **appended to**, not taken from #1303 — that branch's copy predates `node/btoa-atob-on-text` and replaces those tests, so taking it wholesale would have silently deleted live coverage.

## Both checks see-it-fail, and a consumer shape for each

Neither check had been watched failing — only passing, which proves nothing for a guard asserting silence. Recorded in the second commit:

- weakening `task-worker-restores-main`'s `RESTORES` pattern to match anything turned **3 of its 6** tests red, the inert-on-a-non-worker case included.
- making `test-discovery-resolves`' `resolvesToFiles` always return `true` turned **3 of node's 14** red — both flagging cases and the resolver's own unit test.

Both landing blocking, so `consumer-safe-change` asks for a migration record or a rehearsal shape. They are additive rather than renaming or requiring anything, so the fixture is the honest answer:

- `growth-member` gains a local task `worker.sh` in the shape the rule scans, correctly restoring `main` before it writes.
- `node-consumer` is new — a member declaring `node` whose `package.json` test script names a glob resolving to a tracked file.

**What that fixture does and doesn't prove:** I mutated the worker fixture to the non-compliant shape and the rehearsal stayed green, so the rehearsal converges the mount rather than executing world-scope rules over it. The shapes prove these rules ride a consumer's mount and the member still converges — not that the rules fire correctly there. The see-it-fail above is what covers firing.

## 9 held back, not asserted

These make claims about external platforms or harness behaviour I could not validate here. Firebase's and Cloudflare's docs are unreachable from this sandbox and Apple's are JS-rendered, so `curl` returns a shell with no content; the harness ones cannot be forced.

- firebase: geohash bounds return candidates, post-filter by haversine
- macos: surface version *and* build number from `Bundle.main`
- cloudflare: choose the storage primitive by access pattern
- cloudflare: hand-declare bindings to dodge the Workers-types/DOM collision
- headless-browser: relay through your fetcher when `curl` reaches a host the browser can't
- unattended-agents: give a research subagent a stopping budget
- unattended-agents: a subagent's "completed" means its turn ended, not that its task finished
- git-github-advanced: "clean status" also covers a PR that triggered no checks at all
- web-scraping: strip `script`/`style`/`noscript` before reading `textContent`

They came from real incidents in real repos, so the evidence exists — it just isn't re-probeable from here. Say the word and I'll land them on that provenance with references entries citing the source PRs.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **3389 pass, 0 fail**
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking**, exit 0
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — 0 bytes, exit 0
- `vendoring/rehearsal/rehearsal.test.mjs` — 72 pass with the two new shapes
- `barrier` caught my own references entry writing a literal `docs/` path — reworded to name `DOCS_DIR` instead of waiving it
- `rule-index.test.mjs` caught five missing README rows, one stale word count, and three over-long row labels

{"number":1798,"title":"Check that the executor workflow passes every declared secret","body":"A secret reaches a task only if `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` names it statically. The wiring converge stamps one env line per declared secret — but `.github/workflows/` is the one directory a converge may not push to, so that file is scaffolded once at adoption and never regenerated. Every task and every invocation endpoint added afterwards declares a secret the job does not carry, and nothing says so until a run reaches the endpoint call.

NoRFinder is that case today: an endpoint declaring `tokenSecret: CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` against an executor whose secrets list is empty, two queue items parked `needs-human-action` (missingbulb/NoRFinder#31 is the member-side fix).

`executor-workflow-secrets` recomputes the expectation from the same two sources the converge reads and reports every name the workflow does not pass. Extra names are not a finding — a member that dropped a task keeps a harmless line.

Advisory, for `conformance-workflow`'s reason: the remedy is a human-merged PR to `.github/workflows/`, the one fix a member's own machinery cannot make, so blocking would turn such a member red with no move of its own to clear it.

Checks run: the new test file (6 tests), the whole suite (one pre-existing failure, `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails loudly because this checkout is shallow), and `check_the_world` — 0 blocking, and the same 103 advisory as before the change. Seen to fire: dropping `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` from this repo's own executor produces the finding, anchored at the marker line.

Closes #1796

{"number":2088,"title":"Read the operator hold from the vars bag, and check that no code reads a repository variable over the REST API","body":"## Problem

Every executor drain in every member logs, after its first item:

```
CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL is not readable live by this run's token (403), so the drain keeps the value it started with …
```

(seen on [missingbulb/Shepherd run 34955548243](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/34955548243/job/104336628795)). `liveSuspendReader` in `hold.mjs` re-read the hold between items over `/repos/{repo}/actions/variables/…`, and the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused on that route in every member — no `permissions:` key grants it. So the read never answered, and the value a run started with was always the one that decided. The executor already carries every repository variable in its vars bag (`CLAUDINITE_VARS`, #1492); nothing else needed the API.

## Change

- **`hold.mjs`** — `isSuspended` reads the hold from the vars bag where the job carries one (the executor), else from the named env copy (the scheduler carries no bag). The header now states what the hold freezes: starts, with a drain already in flight finishing the batch it started with.
- **`loop.mjs`** — the between-items `heldNow` seam and its log line are gone: with no live read there is nothing for it to ask that the first-act gate did not.
- **`github.mjs`** — the REST route is gone. `readRepoVariable` stays exported, answering from the bag in the old `{ status, json }` shape, and so does `liveSuspendReader` — both are names a member's local pack may import (`consumer-safe-change`), so the discharge chosen is the re-export shim, not a migration record.
- **Tests, sim, `PRINCIPLES.md`** — the live-read tests are replaced by one that proves the bag is read (mutated the read to env-only and watched it fail); the sim no longer models a repo-variable route the engine does not call; S37 now asserts that no run *starts* after the hold and that every post-hold evaluation belongs to the drain already in flight.

## The check

`repo-variables-through-the-bag`, declared in `claudinite-tasks` so every member declaring the pack runs it over its own local packs: any `/actions/variables` route in engine or pack code outside tests is a finding. Authored first and watched fire on `github.mjs:276` before the fix; silent on the real tree after it. Blocking after the standard grace window.

## Audit of the tasks

Every canon task worker reads its repository variables as `process.env.NAME`, which `taskEnv` unpacks from the bag additively — that is already the bag path, so no worker changed. The only non-bag access in the tree was the executor's own REST read above.

Each row is a set of rules that only matter while editing a nameable file class (a `paths:`-scoped skill the guard loads) or during one nameable activity (a description-triggered skill). Rules judged always-on discipline are left where they are. Word counts are the file's whole prose today.

|---|---|---|---|
| macos (1891) | the six "holding a device the user can unplug" rules | new `macos-audio-device-lifecycle` | `paths: **/*Audio*.swift, **/*Capture*.swift` |
| macos | the eight signing / notarization / DMG / Gatekeeper rules | new `macos-signing-and-release` | activity: signing or distributing a build; `.github/workflows/*release*` |
| macos | bundle assembly, icon, `LSUIElement`, `LSMinimumSystemVersion` | new `macos-app-bundle` | `paths: **/Info.plist, Package.swift` |
| macos | entitlements and TCC (three rules); speech recognition (three); sleep/wake (three); lifecycle/exit (two) | four small skills | `**/*.entitlements`, `**/Info.plist`; sources using `SFSpeech*` / `NSWorkspace` / `AppDelegate` |

entries.description: Get information about a specific issue in a GitHub repository.

method.description:
The read operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
1. get - Get issue details. Also returns best-effort hierarchy flags (`has_parent`, `has_children`); `parent` and `sub_issues_summary` are optional relationship summaries, and `closed_by_pull_requests` summarizes the pull requests configured to close the issue as `total_count` plus up to 5 `references`.
2. get_comments - Get issue comments.
3. get_sub_issues - Get sub-issues (children) of the issue.
4. get_parent - Get the parent issue, if this issue is a sub-issue of another.
5. get_labels - Get labels assigned to the issue.

{"number":2062,"title":"Halve the test suite: unblock the long pole, cut the per-fixture git spawns","body":"Ran the `ci-performance-evaluation` playbook end to end over this repo's suite. 3667 tests, all green.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **local suite wall clock** (4 cores) | 120.6s, 119.3s | **56.9s, 59.2s, 59.6s** |
| **CI `Unit tests` step** | 116s, 129s | **87s, 74s** |
| serial total, all 301 files | 263.3s | 209.4s |
| the longest single file | 76.5s | 22.4s |
| one `ruleTester` case | 53.2ms | 35.3ms |

CI gains less than local and its own spread is wide on both sides (116-129s before, 74-87s after), so the honest reading is ~1.5x there against ~2.1x here. I have not established the mechanism for the gap and am not going to guess at one — two samples an arm is what the numbers above are worth.

## Where the time actually was

The step breakdown first, over several runs: checkout 9-10s, setup-node 5s, **Unit tests 116-129s**, all three sweeps and both gates together ≤1s. The tests, and nothing else, were the job. No install step and no lockfile, so there is no cache to add.

Locally the suite ran 120.6s wall against 250s of user+sys on 4 cores — **52% utilisation, three cores idle**. Timing every file on its own found why: `vendoring/rehearsal/rehearsal.test.mjs` was **76.5s by itself**, and `node --test` parallelises across *files*. That one file was a floor no number of workers could get under, and it sat above the 66s that perfect 4-core parallelism would give — which is exactly why the suite idled at 120s.

Everything else was not slow tests but one fixed cost: ~1000 tests in a narrow band at ~53ms each, before any rule ran.

## What changed

**1. The rehearsals run concurrently.** The 74 (fixture, mode) rehearsals in that file each spend their wall clock waiting on nine child processes and share nothing — own temp dir, own subprocesses. `step()`/`buildFixture()` become async and the tests sit in a `describe` with a concurrency of 4. Steps *within* one rehearsal stay strictly ordered, each awaiting the last, because each judges what the one before wrote.

File alone **79.1s → 22.1s**. 4 is measured as the knee, not picked: 2 → 38.7s, 4 → 24.2s, 6 → 23.6s, 8 → 24.4s, and the 78.7s of CPU it now spends over 22.1s of wall is 3.6 of 4 cores. Proven still able to fail: pointing a step at a missing module turns the rehearsals red with the failing step's output intact.

**2. The per-fixture cost.** A `ruleTester` case was 17 git subprocesses before a single rule ran; two of them are the fixture's own content and the rest are identical every time.
- `makeRepo` seeds one template repo per process and copies it. `git init` + seed commit + feature branch is byte-identical for every fixture with an empty `base` — nearly all of them — and a file copy is ~3ms against ~27ms of subprocesses. The template is pruned of the ten files git writes there and never reads back (the hook samples above all), which was four fifths of the copy.
- `resolveBaseRef` asked `rev-parse --verify` once per candidate, so a repo based on a local `main` — every fixture, and any clone with no remote — paid two `origin/` misses before its answer. `cat-file --batch-check` answers all four on stdin in one spawn, through the same revision parser.

makeRepo 23.4ms → 11.4ms, buildContext 28.9ms → 23.3ms.

Behaviour-identical rather than assumed to be: the whole context — every field, file contents, added lines, the vendored set — hashes the same through both seeding paths across eight fixture shapes in both scopes; and `cat-file` agrees with `rev-parse` on every ambiguity that separates them (a tag sharing a branch's name, a remote ref with no local branch, both spellings present, the canon checkout itself).

## A real bug the faster suite surfaced

One A/B run went red on `--list emits the machine-readable rule catalog`. Not a flake: the catalog was cut off after the `t` rules, missing exactly the last 8. On **pristine `origin/main`**, with six cores busy, **15 of 60 `spawnSync` callers got a partial catalog** — status 0, empty stderr, a silently short answer on the channel whose whole purpose is being machine-read.

The cause is `process.exit()` over a pipe: every caller that *captures* output gets one, a Node pipe write is asynchronous, and `process.exit()` drops what is still queued. Both check runners now set `process.exitCode` and let the process end, which flushes; the world runner's branches become an if/else chain since an exit code does not stop the script, and the catalog goes out as one write. Under the identical load, **60 of 60 now return the full catalog**.

The same hazard sits on ~120 further `process.exit` call sites that print first — selftest, converge-wiring, the migration runner. That sweep is #2065 rather than widened into this PR.

## Left alone deliberately

- **Merging `buildContext`'s two `git diff --name-only` calls into one `--name-status`** — worth ~3ms a case, but the two disagree on rename entries in ways a fixture would not show, and that is not worth a subtle scoping bug.
- **Making `ctx.commits` / `ctx.branch` lazy** — another ~5ms a case. Real, but the suite is now within ~10% of its 4-core floor, so it buys single-digit seconds against a change to engine code every member runs.
- The 1562 tests that already run in under 1ms are 0.1% of the suite. They are fine, and this says so, so nobody re-profiles them.

{"number":1667,"title":"Rules → skills: the audit's path-forced extractions; description-triggered ones stay prose","body":"Applies #1662 under the owner's bar (set mid-review): a rule leaves `RULES.md` for a skill only where that skill's `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` covers **every** moment the rule is needed. A skill the model would have to pick by description alone is not predictable, so those rules stay in the prose. The first twelve commits moved everything the audit named; the last commit derives the prose back from `main` for everything that had only a description trigger, leaving the fourteen path-forced skills.

**What stays extracted** (all forced by the guard for the files named):

| Pack | Skill | Forced for |
|---|---|---|
| basics | `writing-repo-scanning-checks` | `**/engine/checks/**`, `**/packs/*/worldRules/**`, `**/packs/*/workRules/**`, `**/packs/*/skills/*/checks.mjs`, `**/declared-checks.json` |
| basics | `working-with-generated-files` | `**/*GENERATED*` |
| executable-requirements | `write-a-requirement-leaf`, `write-a-saga`, `deterministic-expecteds` | `dev/requirements/requirements.md`, `dev/requirements/saga/**`, `dev/requirements/**/cases/**` + `shared/**` |
| firebase | `firestore-security-rules`, `firebase-functions`; `create-release-plan` gains `.firebaserc`, `firebase.json` | `**/firestore.rules`, `**/storage.rules`; `functions/**` |
| aws-sam | `sam-template`, `sam-build-and-deps` | `**/template.yaml`, `**/template.yml`; `package.json` + template |
| flutter | `flutter-golden-tests`, `flutter-pubspec` | `**/*_test.dart`, `**/test/**/*.dart`; `**/pubspec.yaml`, `**/pubspec.lock` |
| macos | `macos-app-bundle` (the two plist keys), `macos-entitlements-and-tcc` | `**/Info.plist`, `**/Package.swift`; `**/*.entitlements`, `**/Info.plist` |
| chrome-extension | `extension-host-permissions` | `**/manifest.json` |
| claudinite-fleet-sheepdog | `configuring-the-fleet` | `.claudinite-settings.json` |
| node | `node-test-discovery` | `.github/workflows/**`, `package.json`, `*/package.json` |
| python | `python-optional-deps` gains the extra-declaration rule | `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `setup.py` (root or one down) |
| static-website | `static-site-releases` gains the managed-copies rule | its existing `.github/site.config`, `static-site-*` workflows |

Rules whose moment no file edit predicts stayed in or returned to `RULES.md` even where a sibling rule was forced: the bundle build-script rules and the Hardened-Runtime flag (macos), pixel-golden capture code (headless-browser), content-script module loading (chrome-extension), the port-boundary design (flutter), the `# noqa: F401` probe (python), "the version moves with the change" (static-website), the deploy-time SAM failures.

**Also kept from the audit's flagged list**: the four stubs (ios, android, app-store-release, play-store-release) lose their `RULES.md`, the stub note now in a README each; describe-only prose moved to READMEs (executable-requirements' line regex and gate inventory, spec-driven-product's gallery pointer, flutter's web-sandbox SDK note, web-scraping's cache/raw-record rationale, macos' notarized-build line).

**Also in this PR**: `packs/claudinite-growth` had two `VERSIONS.md` rows claiming 60903.5 on `main`, which `pack-version-claimed-once` blocks on every tree; the second row takes 60903.6 and the manifest follows.

**Verification**: full suite `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3187 pass, 1 fail (`engine-pack-lane-shims`, which refuses to run on this shallow clone; not this change). `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` are clean. Every touched pack README's rule table was reconciled 1:1 against its `RULES.md`; the skills index and pack directory were regenerated.

Closes #1662

content.text: {"number":1575,"title":"Recover the rationale #467 cut from the shared packs into references.md","body":"Follow-up to #1567, which did this for the local pack. Same question asked of the **shared canon packs**. Closes #1571 ## What the history actually shows Mining every commit that shrank a still-standing canon rule found **49 shrink events, 43 on rules that still stand**. They resolve to one seam and two false positives: | Commit | Verdict | |---|---| | **#467 `2f3e4e9a`** — "Tighten every RULES.md to when + what + one non-obvious fact" | The only genuine seam | | #853 | **Relocated, not lost** — the text lives at `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:44` | | #451 | **Converted** — became the `firebase/functions-predeploy-build` check, whose source quotes the removed sentence | #467's own commit message states what it cut: *"consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it"*. That was July 2026 — **before a `references.md` existed to hold it** (the convention landed in `a13cf4e2`, three commits ago). So recovering it doesn't undo the owner's decision, it completes it: every rule line stays exactly as #467 left it, and the reason moves to the doc built for it. The same message confirms the incident narratives and `#NNN` citations were shed from **the local pack only** — which is what #1567 already recovered. The canon's losses are pure rationale. ## What was recovered — 25 entries across 8 packs Only clauses carrying a **failure mode, cost, frequency, or authority** — something a review can actually weigh. {"number":1634,"title":"Every pack's RULES.md carries rules, not a description of the pack","body":"Closes #1632

The same audit #1625 got, across the other 25 packs. Every one opened its `RULES.md` with a paragraph describing what the pack covers ("Portable, project-agnostic practices for …", "This document defines how the owner wants … run"), and several framed their sections the same way. It changes nothing a session does, every session in every declaring repo pays for it, and each pack's `README.md` plus its manifest's `ruleRoutingGuidance` (what renders into `directory.GENERATED.md`) already carries it — I checked each one before dropping it.

**Dropped:** 25 intro paragraphs; the playbook framing in `research-project` and `spec-driven-product` (what the class is, "a default to adapt, not a contract"); `basics`'s four section preambles, including the skill list the session's own skill roster already carries; `headless-browser`'s scope note; `macos`'s "these are the rules that cost the most to learn" and "Two consequences"; `node`'s "Two that recur".

**Kept as rules, re-keyed:** `macos`'s usage-description paragraph becomes **Reaching for a protected resource**; `research-project`'s interaction-cadence paragraph becomes two bullets; `python`'s three section-shaped rules become trigger-keyed bullets at the ration (280 → 150 words).

**Left alone:** the paragraph-form instruction in `executable-requirements` and `research-project` — it is prose-shaped, but it instructs, and rewriting it is a rewrite of substance rather than this sweep. Corpus non-rule prose is 2,900 → 1,080 words, and what remains is nearly all of that kind. Those two, plus `spec-driven-product`, read as manuals whose procedure would sit better in a skill; worth a separate look.

Pack READMEs take the two new rule rows (`macos`, `research-project`) and recounted word columns where a dropped preamble had been counted into a rule. Every touched pack bumps its version with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

{"number":401,"title":"Pack adoption: interview-in-manifest, adopt-pack skill, enforcing check","body":"Closes #400.

Makes adopting a pack a first-class, interviewed act instead of a per-request improvisation.

## What

- **`adopt-pack` skill** (`packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-pack/`) — the narrow flow for turning packs on in an already-adopted member: declare → run each added pack's adoption interview and record answers → re-vendor → scaffold what the pack now demands → land through the review gate. Whole-repo bootstrap/refresh stays `adopt-claudinite`.
- **`adoption-answers-pending`** — a work-scope, blocking check: a pack *newly declared on the branch* must record an answer for every adoption question it asks. Reuses `interviewState` (so `via`-materialized dependencies ask nothing) and only fires for packs added in this branch (a pack already in the base is never re-litigated). This reconciles an enforcing "check-the-work" with the existing design where a *pending* answer is only a mild SessionStart note — nightly/unattended runs never block. Adds `packs`/`config` accessors to the fluent `work` context.
- **`product-wiki` questions** — `product`, `users`, `market`, recorded as intent (the pack takes no config); they scope which wikis get seeded and what the competitor research measures against.
- **`executable-requirements` questions** — `ui_testing` (the UI-test harness / visual-golden path) and `requirements_source` (existing doc / issue tracker / fresh → `config.spec`).
- **`executable-requirements` standard** — two conventions made explicit: the requirement line stays a scannable one-liner with expanded detail collapsed behind a `<details>` block (clean GitHub review), and kind selection favors the **simplest owner verification** — a short test driving to a state plus a visual golden the owner checks by sight — maximizing the share of requirements verified by looking.

## Why

Adopting `product-wiki` without knowing the users/market/product yields a hollow skeleton; adopting `executable-requirements` without deciding the UI-test mechanism and requirements source defers the two choices that shape every requirement. Baking the questions into the manifests and enforcing answers on the adding branch puts the interview where the owner is present.

## Testing

- Fixture tests for the new check: added-unanswered blocks; fully answered is clean; a pack already in the base stays silent; a `via`-only dependency asks nothing.
- Manifest assertions for both packs' new questions.
- Full suite green (556 tests); world sweep 0 blocking; work green.

{"number":185,"title":"flutter/node pack detect: match monorepo subdir markers","body":"## What

A lessons-learned improvement surfaced while landing #165 in the ShoutsAndWhispers consumer.

The `flutter` and `node` packs fingerprinted a **repo-root** `pubspec.yaml` / `package.json`. A monorepo that keeps its Flutter app in `app/` and its Node functions in `functions/` (exactly ShoutsAndWhispers' layout) therefore failed `detect()`, and the consumer had to declare the pack **plus** an `accept`-with-reason just to satisfy the `pack-declaration` check.

Now `detect()` matches the marker at the repo root **or one directory down** — a monorepo's `app/` / `functions/` / `server/` dir — but **never deeper**, so a stray `pubspec.yaml`/`package.json` in a nested example or fixture tree can't trip detection. This mirrors the `android`/`ios` packs, which already match subdir markers (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `ios/Runner/Info.plist`).

## Verification

- New `checks/test/pack-detect.test.mjs` — 5 cases per pack: marker at root, one directory down (monorepo), two-or-more deep (must NOT match), no marker, and basename-only (`pubspec.yaml.bak` must NOT match).
- Full unit suite: **87/87** pass.
- `node checks/run.mjs` conformance sweep: clean.

## Follow-up (separate repo)

Once this ships and ShoutsAndWhispers re-syncs its `.claudinite/`, flutter/node will detect there and the `accept`-with-reason in its `.claudinite-checks.json` becomes an inert no-op (there's no stale-acceptance check, so it's harmless) — can be cleaned up opportunistically.

Closes #184
