## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-1)
- **Reason:** The failure mode is a reader trapped mid-page: a map that is not the whole viewport
  but grabs the wheel captures a scroll that was meant for the document. Recovered from the rule's
  own pre-#467 text (cut by 2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling
  it”, before this pack had a references.md to hold it).
- **Mechanism:** prose
- **Retire when:** Reaffirm while the map is embedded mid-page; retire for a full-viewport map,
  where wheel-zoom is the expected behaviour.
## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-2)
- **Reason:** The ground is a licence term, not taste: OpenStreetMap's tile-usage policy requires
  visible attribution, so stripping the `attribution` string while tidying the UI breaks the
  licence. The companion `maxZoom: 19` matches the real ceiling of OSM's tiles, so Leaflet does not
  request levels the provider does not serve. Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467 text (cut by
  2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it”, before this pack
  had a references.md to hold it).
- **Mechanism:** prose
- **Retire when:** Reaffirm against the current OSM tile-usage policy and its zoom ceiling; retire
  only for a provider whose terms differ.
@@@@@@ README
# leaflet pack

Active when the repo references [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/) — a CDN asset (`leaflet@` / `leaflet.js` / `leaflet.css`) in HTML, or an `L.map` / `L.tileLayer` / `L.markerClusterGroup` call in JS/TS source. Mostly prose (these are runtime behaviours with no clean static signature); the CDN wiring of the assets themselves is written into the HTML, and a tile layer's attribution is written into its options object, so those are checks.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feature-detect a plugin, fall back to core | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| An embedded map sets scrollWheelZoom false | medium | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Keep the tile provider's attribution | critical | legal | prose: <100 words + check (`leaflet/tile-attribution`) |
| Transform a marker's inner element | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |

Provenance: distilled from `missingbulb/EdFringeNow` (the "Fringe Discover" static site — `index.html` CDN wiring and `js/app.js` map/marker/cluster code), the first fleet member seen using Leaflet.

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `leaflet/asset-integrity` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `leaflet/tile-attribution` | critical | legal | check: blocking |
@@@@@ pack.mjs

// Leaflet pack: portable runtime gotchas for the Leaflet web-mapping library
// (map init, tile layers, markers/divIcons, and CDN-loaded plugins like
// Leaflet.markercluster). Most are runtime behaviours with no repo-state
// signature and stay prose; the CDN wiring of the assets themselves is written
// into the HTML, and a tile layer's attribution is written into its own options
// object, so those convert. Fingerprinted by an actual Leaflet reference: a
// CDN asset (leaflet@ / leaflet.js / leaflet.css) in HTML, or a Leaflet API call
// site (L.map( / L.tileLayer( / L.markerClusterGroup() ) in source. The marker
// only *suspects* the pack; declaring it is the project's call, like every pack.

const LEAFLET_ASSET = /\bleaflet(\.js|\.css|@[\d.]|[-/]dist)/i;
const LEAFLET_API = /\bL\.(map|tileLayer|markerClusterGroup)\s*\(/;
const SOURCE = /\.(html?|mjs|cjs|jsx?|tsx?)$/;

export default {
  version: '60920.1',
  minEngineVersion: '60822.1',
  ruleRoutingGuidance: {
    belongs: 'map rendering with the Leaflet library — map init options, tile layers, markers and divIcons, CDN plugin pinning',
    excludes: 'generic HTML markup rules — that is html; non-map dependency policy belongs to node',
  },
  marker: 'a Leaflet reference (CDN asset, or an L.map/L.tileLayer/L.markerClusterGroup call) in HTML/JS source',
  detect: (ctx) =>
    ctx.tracked.some((f) => {
      if (!SOURCE.test(f)) return false;
      const text = ctx.read(f);
      return text !== null && (LEAFLET_ASSET.test(text) || LEAFLET_API.test(text));
    }),
};
@@@@@ RULES
# Leaflet

- **Feature-detect an optional Leaflet plugin before using it, and fall back to core when its CDN
  script didn't load.** A plugin's separate `<script>` (markercluster, heat, draw, …) can silently
  fail to load while the base Leaflet bundle succeeds, leaving `L.markerClusterGroup` (etc.)
  undefined. Guard the call with `typeof L.markerClusterGroup === "function"` and add markers
  straight to the map when it's absent — the base map must still render. (feature-detect-optional)

- **Default an embedded, mid-page map to `scrollWheelZoom: false` so it doesn't hijack the page
  scroll.** Construct it with `L.map(el, { scrollWheelZoom: false })`, or gate wheel-zoom behind a
  click/focus. (default-embedded-mid)

- **Keep the tile provider's attribution — it's a licence term, not decoration.** The
  `attribution: '… © OpenStreetMap contributors'` on the `L.tileLayer(...)` must stay even when
  tidying the UI. Set `maxZoom` to the provider's real ceiling (OSM tiles top out at 19) so Leaflet
  doesn't request zoom levels the provider doesn't serve. (keep-tile-providers)

- **When a marker needs its own CSS `transform`, put it on an inner element, not the `divIcon`
  root.** Leaflet positions every marker by writing an inline `transform: translate3d(...)` onto the
  icon's root element, clobbering any `transform` you set there on the next reposition. Make the
  icon root a zero-size anchor (`iconSize: [0, 0]`, `iconAnchor: [0, 0]`) and apply your
  rotation/centring transform to a `<span>` inside its `html`. (marker-needs-css)

```entry _pack
- **Reason:** the theme is one, keep the importable core dependency-free and gate every heavy thing
  behind an optional extra, and it is portable across any package built around an ML model, a native
  audio or GPU library or a cloud SDK. What splits the pack is where each rule can be judged: the
  repo's own `pyproject.toml` names exactly which packages are optional, so a top-level import of a
  self-declared-optional package is a false-positive-free file-scoped signal and mechanizes; which
  deps count as heavy, whether an interface warrants a stdlib mock, and whether an import is a
  genuine availability probe are architecture judgment with no such signature and stay prose.
```

@@ -2,7 +2,6 @@
 
 - **A published file is a file the publish set names — adding a page is two edits.** The Pages artifact is assembled from `.github/site.config`'s `publish_paths` and nothing else, so a new page, stylesheet or data file that isn't under a published path (or named in the list) is simply absent from the live site, with no error anywhere: the build is green, the deploy succeeds, the page 404s. When you add a file the site serves, put it under an already-published directory or add it to `publish_paths` in the same change. The list is additive on purpose — the alternative, "publish the repo minus what we remember to exclude", publishes every draft, note and key nobody thought to hide.
 - **The version moves with the change.** A change touching the published site raises `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` in the same PR — `node .github/actions/bump-site-version/bump.mjs $(version_files)` computes it from the previous version and the UTC date, and `sw/version-bumped` is what holds the line. Never hand-write the `ymmdd` or the counter: a typed value either collides with a released one or is dated in the future, and the next bump refuses. The release flow writes no version of its own — it ships what it finds on `main` — so a shipped change without a bump is never released at all. The one deliberate human part is the **major**, a "this is a new generation of the site" statement; the owner's **"bump version"** means exactly that, and the release workflow's `bump: major` dispatch is what performs it.
-- **The pipeline files under `.github/workflows/static-site-*` and `.github/actions/{read-site-config,bump-site-version,assemble-site}` are managed copies of the pack's `stubs/`.** Fix the pack and re-vendor; an edit to the copy is overwritten and, until it is, makes this repo's pipeline differ from every other site repo's. The repo's own values all live in `.github/site.config`, which is what the copies read.
 - **The site is served from a subpath, not a domain root.** GitHub Pages serves it at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/` (unless a custom domain is configured), so a root-relative URL — `/style.css`, `/img/logo.png`, a `fetch('/data.json')` — resolves above the site and 404s in production while working fine in a local `file://` or `python -m http.server` preview. Write links, asset paths and fetches **relative** to the page.
 - **Freshness is a published manifest's job, not a per-file TTL's.** There is no server here to vary `Cache-Control` per file, so the freshness policy moves into the client — and the shape it reaches for first, giving each file a lifetime matching how fast you think it changes, reprices the same bet on every file and gets it wrong in both directions at once: too long and visitors read stale data, too short and they re-download what never changed. Publish one small manifest naming every downloadable asset and a hash of its contents, fetch *that* on each load, and evict exactly the entries whose hash moved. It buys longer caching **and** fresher data, which no TTL can offer together, and the extra request is the one you are probably already making for a version string. Expect a mismatch mid-deploy — the manifest is fetched, a deploy lands, the asset that follows disagrees — so refetch once and carry on; only a disagreement that survives fresh copies of both is a fault worth surfacing.
 - **Nothing can attest to its own freshness, and size attests to nothing at all.** A stale file carries a perfectly valid hash *of itself*, and an internal `"version"` field states which generation it is, never whether that generation is still current — so the expected hash has to come from a file fetched fresher than the one being judged, which is what makes the manifest the one asset that may never carry a TTL of its own. Caching it saves no round-trip; it moves the staleness up a level and hides it better. Nor is length a cheap stand-in for a hash: a correction applied uniformly across a file is routinely byte-length-neutral — a timezone fix rewriting every `16:25` to `17:25` moved **0 bytes** of a 3.1 MB catalogue while changing the meaning of every record in it. And record the manifest's hash beside the entry as you write it, so the check is a string compare; re-hashing the stored body means pushing megabytes through a digest on the critical path of every load to answer a question the bookkeeping already knows.

# Leaflet

Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/) web-mapping library — loading it from a CDN, embedding a map in a page, and the marker/`divIcon` and plugin behaviours that bite regardless of which app renders the map. True for any Leaflet map read cold.

- **Load Leaflet — and every Leaflet plugin — from a version-pinned CDN URL with a Subresource-Integrity hash and `crossorigin`.** Pin the exact version (`leaflet@1.9.4`, not `@latest`) and carry `integrity="sha256-…"` + `crossorigin=""` on both the CSS `<link>` and the JS `<script>`, so an upgraded or tampered CDN asset can't silently change under the app. The trap is doing this for the core bundle but forgetting a plugin: pin and hash the plugin the same way, or the one un-pinned `<script>` is the hole. (Grounded in `index.html`, which pins+SRIs `leaflet@1.9.4` core yet loaded `leaflet.markercluster@1.5.3` without an `integrity` attribute — the inconsistency is the lesson.)

- **Feature-detect an optional Leaflet plugin before using it, and fall back to core when its CDN script didn't load.** A separate `<script>` for a plugin (markercluster, heat, draw, …) can silently fail to load while the base Leaflet bundle succeeds, leaving `L.markerClusterGroup` (etc.) undefined. Guard the call with `typeof L.markerClusterGroup === "function"` and, when it's absent, add markers straight to the map instead of throwing — the base map must still render. (Grounded in `js/app.js` `renderMarkers()`: the cluster group is created only behind the `typeof` guard, and each marker falls back to `marker.addTo(map)` when the plugin is unavailable.)

- **Default an embedded, mid-page map to `scrollWheelZoom: false` so it doesn't hijack the page scroll.** A map that isn't the whole viewport but grabs the wheel traps a reader who scrolls onto it. Construct it with `L.map(el, { scrollWheelZoom: false })` (or gate wheel-zoom behind a click/focus). (Grounded in `js/app.js` `initMap()`: `L.map("leaflet-map", { scrollWheelZoom: false })`.)

- **Keep the tile provider's attribution — it's a licence term, not decoration.** OpenStreetMap's tile-usage policy requires visible attribution, so the `attribution: '… © OpenStreetMap contributors'` on the `L.tileLayer(...)` must stay even when tidying the UI; stripping it breaks the licence. Set `maxZoom` to the provider's real ceiling (OSM tiles top out at 19) so Leaflet doesn't request zoom levels the provider doesn't serve. (Grounded in `js/app.js` `initMap()`: the OSM `tileLayer` carries the attribution string and `maxZoom: 19`.)

- **When a marker needs its own CSS `transform`, put it on an inner element, not the `divIcon` root — Leaflet writes an inline `transform` on the icon root to position it.** Leaflet positions every marker by writing an inline `transform: translate3d(...)` onto the icon's root element; a `transform` you set on that same root (to rotate or centre the glyph) is clobbered on the next reposition. Make the icon root a zero-size anchor (`iconSize: [0, 0]`, `iconAnchor: [0, 0]`) and apply your rotation/centring transform to a `<span>` inside its `html`, whose transform Leaflet never touches. (Grounded in `js/app.js`: the route arrowhead rotates an inner `.route-arrow` span, and the arrival-check pin uses a zero-size anchor root with the visible pill as an inner span, exactly to survive Leaflet's root transform.)

content.content:
# site-release — what the worker does

Deploys the default branch to GitHub Pages and, where the public-website pack is
declared, records the version that went out first. There is no `task.md` because
there is no agent: a release is a version number, a push, a dispatch and a wait, and
none of the four is a judgment call.

The operating knowledge — how to force one, how to roll one back, what is on the
GitHub side and what a park means — is the
[github-pages-pipeline](../../skills/github-pages-pipeline/SKILL.md) skill. This file
is only what the worker does.

## The run

1. **Read the branch tip.** The publish set comes from `.github/site.config` as the
   remote has it, never from the executor's checkout, and every path it names is
   checked against that commit's tree — so a release never dispatches a build that
   fails on a path the config names.
2. **Advance and stamp, if there is a version to advance.** The worker imports
   public-website's `public/version.mjs` from beside this pack on the mount. Present,
   it hands back the files a bump rewrites — the record and every page carrying the
   stamp — and the worker commits them. Absent (the pack undeclared), the release is
   the tip as found, and the run says so.
3. **Push the bump to the default branch**, rebuilding on whatever landed underneath
   and retrying — the scheduler and the maintenance PRs land there too, and a lost
   race would leave the repo naming an older version than the one being served.
4. **Dispatch the vendored [deploy workflow](../../stubs/workflows/github-pages-deploy.yml)
   at that exact commit and wait for its run.** The run is found as the workflow's
   newest dispatch created after ours; a run that ends in anything but success parks
   with its URL.
5. **Probe the site.** The Pages URL is fetched and its status reported, along with
   whether the page already shows the version just cut. Pages propagates for a minute
   or so, so a stale stamp is reported, never parked.

The bump lands **before** the deploy on purpose. Both halves can fail, and only one
of the two drifts is silent: a site serving a version the repo has no record of. A
version number consumed by a release whose deploy then failed is visible in the park
and costs nothing — the next release takes the next number.

## Why the declaration reads as it does

**A workflow, dispatched.** A Pages deploy has to be one: its publish steps are
marketplace actions, and no task can invoke a `uses:` step. So the task owns the
trigger and the decision to run, and the workflow carries only the deploy — dispatch
only, no push trigger, so nothing deploys behind the task. Dispatching it with the
executor's own token is the one event kind that token *does* fire a workflow for.

**`unreleased-commits`** ([`preconditions.mjs`](preconditions.mjs)) is the task's own
term because no built-in asks a release's question. The file says why the two nearest
built-ins are both wrong here, and what the gate degrades to on a repo with no version.

**`on_interrupt: needs-human`** because a release is a one-shot external effect: a
reclaimed claim must not re-run it, spend a second version number and redeploy.

**No `code_work_required_secrets`.** The deploy runs on the workflow job's own
identity and the bump on the executor's token; nothing here needs a secret a repo
has to configure.

**`expected_outcome: no_code_changes`** — the run opens no pull request. It does
commit, but to the default branch directly: a version bump reviewed after the fact is
a review of a number a machine derived, and holding the release for it would mean the
site lags the repo by however long the PR sits.

**Daily.** A release goes out the night after anything lands, and a night with
nothing to release files no run at all.

-- **Load Leaflet — and every Leaflet plugin — from a version-pinned CDN URL with a Subresource-Integrity hash and `crossorigin`.** Pin the exact version (`leaflet@1.9.4`, not `@latest`) and carry `integrity="sha256-…"` + `crossorigin=""` on both the CSS `<link>` and the JS `<script>`, so an upgraded or tampered CDN asset can't silently change under the app. The trap is doing this for the core bundle but forgetting a plugin: pin and hash the plugin the same way, or the one un-pinned `<script>` is the hole. Guard the call with `typeof L.markerClusterGroup === "function"` and, when it's absent, add markers straight to the map instead of throwing — the base map must still render. {"number":403,"title":"Pack discovery: add leaflet pack (from EdFringeNow)","body":"## Growth — pack discovery

Weekly pack-discovery run against member **`missingbulb/EdFringeNow`**. First fleet sighting of an unhomed, load-bearing technology: **Leaflet** (web mapping). Authoring its pack on first sight.

## Why a pack

EdFringeNow's "Fringe Discover" static site renders an interactive Leaflet map of Fringe venues — Leaflet + the Leaflet.markercluster plugin loaded from unpkg (`index.html`), with the map/marker/cluster logic in `js/app.js`. No canon pack owns Leaflet, and its usage yields real, portable gotchas (not the edfringe-specific scraping, which is this member's one-off).

## What's in it (all grounded + cited, no padding)

Prose-only pack (runtime/asset-wiring behaviours with no clean static signature). Five rules, each traced to real EdFringeNow usage:

1. **Pin + SRI every Leaflet asset** — core is pinned+hashed, the markercluster plugin was loaded without `integrity`; the inconsistency is the lesson (`index.html`).
2. **Feature-detect an optional plugin, fall back to core** — `typeof L.markerClusterGroup === "function"` guard + plain-marker fallback when the plugin CDN fails (`js/app.js` `renderMarkers()`).
3. **Embedded map defaults to `scrollWheelZoom: false`** so it doesn't hijack page scroll (`js/app.js` `initMap()`).
4. **Keep OSM tile attribution (licence term) + real `maxZoom`** (`js/app.js` `initMap()`).
5. **Put a marker's own `transform` on an inner span, not the `divIcon` root** — Leaflet writes an inline transform on the root (`js/app.js` route arrow / arrival-check pin).

## Fingerprint

`detect` fires on a Leaflet CDN asset (`leaflet@` / `leaflet.js` / `leaflet.css`) in HTML or an `L.map` / `L.tileLayer` / `L.markerClusterGroup` call in JS/TS source — verified true on EdFringeNow and correctly quiet on a Leaflet-free repo / a markdown-only mention.

## Write surface

Bounded to `packs/leaflet/` (`pack.mjs`, `RULES.md`, `README.md`) + the `packs/README.md` catalog row. World sweep: **0 blocking** (4 pre-existing file-placement advisories on unrelated engine files); `catalog-completeness` passes.

Refs #303

{"number":510,"title":"prose-to-checks: convert the Leaflet CDN pin + SRI rule to a check","body":"Daily `prose-to-checks-sweep` run for 2026-07-28 (dispatched by #504; ledger #450).

## What converted

**`packs/leaflet/RULES.md`** — *"Load Leaflet — and every Leaflet plugin — from a version-pinned CDN URL with a Subresource-Integrity hash and `crossorigin`"* → **`leaflet/asset-integrity`** (blocking).

It passes the check-the-world test cleanly: the thing the rule constrains — the CDN wiring of the assets — is written into the page's own `<script>` / `<link>` tags, a static signature a post-hoc scan sees directly. Nothing about it is in-flight or judgment.

The prose bullet is gone; the failure message owns the rule now (what / why / fix / `doc:` back to `packs/leaflet/RULES.md`).

## Parsed, not grepped

Grepping for `unpkg.com` or for a missing `integrity` answers the wrong question. The rule is about one *tag*, so the scan reads each `<script>`/`<link>`'s own attributes and judges only those:

- only a tag whose **own** `src`/`href` is a **remote** URL naming a Leaflet asset is judged;
- HTML comments are blanked first (newlines kept, so line numbers hold);
- an exact pin means a `major.minor…` reached by the URL's own delimiters (`leaflet@1.9.4/…`, `/leaflet/1.9.4/…`, `leaflet-1.9.4.js`) — `@latest` and a major-only `@1` are not pins;
- the finding names *which* of pin / `integrity` / `crossorigin` is missing, so a half-wired tag gets a precise message.

Quiet by construction: a locally vendored `js/leaflet.js`, a `preconnect` to the CDN host, a non-Leaflet CDN script, a Leaflet URL sitting in page text or in a JS string, and an example written inside an HTML comment.

## See-it-fail

`packs-tests/leaflet/pack.test.mjs` — 6 fixtures:

- **fires**: the plugin `<script>` left bare beside a correctly wired core bundle (the exact trap the prose named), and `@latest` / a version-less URL (asserting the finding names the pin);
- **clean**: core + plugin both pinned and hashed, across unpkg and cdnjs URL shapes;
- **FP guards**: vendored/same-origin asset + preconnect, non-Leaflet CDN tag + Leaflet URL in text and in a JS string, and the HTML-comment case.

Both firing fixtures were verified red with the rule's `run` neutered to `return []`, then the check restored — the four guards and the clean case stayed green throughout, so they prove the scoping rather than the absence of a scan.

## Verification

- Full offline suite (the CI test roots): **786 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking, 7 advisory** — the same seven pre-existing `file-placement` advisories on `engine/` that main carries; no new findings.
- The `leaflet` pack is not declared in this repo, so the new rule doesn't run on the canon's own sweep; the fixture test is its proof.

## Considered and deliberately left as prose

- **leaflet: keep the tile provider's attribution + a real `maxZoom`.** A licence term and a genuine static-ish signature, but `attribution` can legitimately be supplied away from the `L.tileLayer(...)` call (`attributionControl.addAttribution`, a shared options constant), so a confident detection isn't available without guessing. Left as prose rather than shipped shaky.
- **leaflet: feature-detect an optional plugin / embedded map defaults to `scrollWheelZoom: false` / `divIcon` transform on an inner span** — runtime and layout-intent behaviours with no artifact signature.
- **html, node** — parser/jsdom divergence knowledge, visible only at runtime.
- **research-project, spec-driven-product, flutter (toolchain, goldens)** — process and judgment, or needing an arbitrary threshold.
- **android, ios, play-store-release** — stubs, no rules captured yet.

Outcome ceiling for this task is `open-pr`: for owner review, **not** to be merged or auto-merged by automation.

Refs #504, #450

```entry writing-link-asset
  default rather than as an absolute.

  one that serves from the repo subpath.
```

```entry _pack
## 2026-09-18 · born · Split the website packs by ownership: public-website, github-pages, cloudflare-site (#2101)
- **Reason:** `static-website` conflated what is true of a static site with what is true of one
  served from GitHub Pages, so a repo hosting its site anywhere else could take only half the pack,
  and the half it left behind was where three of the four checks lived. The serving half becomes
  its own pack, rebuilt in the shape `cloudflare-site`'s release already had: a Pages deploy is
  made of marketplace actions only a workflow job can run, so that is all the one vendored workflow
  carries, dispatch-only, and everything else about a release is the `site-release` task. Four
  workflows and three composite actions become one workflow and two scripts; the GitHub Release,
  the tag and the bump dispatch go with the versions they carried, which are `public-website`'s
  now. The pack names no other host: a site is served from Pages or from something else, never
  both.
- **Mechanism:** the pack manifest, fingerprinted by `.github/site.config`, the pack's own central
  artifact, and requiring `claudinite-tasks` because the release is a work item rather than a
  workflow.
```
```entry github-pages-pipeline
## 2026-09-18 · moved · Name the Pages skill for what it does, and cut it to the actions (#2101)
- **Reason:** it does not perform a release; it wires, changes and debugs the vendored pipeline
  that does. Halved with the pack it came from: the stage-by-stage narrative of the publish
  reusable is that file's own header comment, and what the pack does and does not own is the
  README's. What is left is the three steps that wire a repo, a table of the four things anyone
  actually drives it to do, and the two facts that surprise people, that the pipeline writes no
  version of its own and that a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push fires no workflow.
- **Mechanism:** the skill moves to `github-pages` as `github-pages-pipeline`, its description
  naming the moments that want it, its path trigger repointed at the renamed workflows and the
  task's files.
```
```entry writing-link-asset
## 2026-09-18 · moved · Split the GitHub Pages half of static-website into a github-pages pack (#2101)
- **Reason:** the subpath is a fact about how Pages serves a site, not about being a website, so it
  goes with the serving half. It is the one rule `static-website` genuinely lost in the split.
- **Mechanism:** prose in this pack's `RULES.md`.
```
```entry writing-link-asset
## 2026-09-18 · reworded · Cut both packs' rules to the ration, evidence into references.md (#2101)
- **Reason:** the rule ran 150 to 200 words where the format asks for one sentence near 40, and
  opened on a state of the world rather than on the act that brings a reader to it. It is now keyed
  to writing the link and carries only the consequence needed to apply it under pressure; nothing
  is weakened and nothing is strengthened, and the rationale moves to the pack's `references.md`.
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
```
```entry wanting-site-deployed
## 2026-09-18 · born · Rebuild github-pages as a nightly release task over one deploy workflow (#2101)
- **Reason:** the `site-release` task is the one path to production because the queue owns the
  trigger, the gate, the version cut and the park lanes. A second publisher has none of them: it
  ships a tree with no version cut, and its green run looks exactly like success while a red one in
  the Actions list reaches nobody.
- **Rejected:** a workflow that publishes on push, which is the shape the pack had until this
  change and the shape a session reaches for first.
- **Mechanism:** prose carrying the wake command, because a session that wants the site deployed
  now would otherwise reach for a push or a dispatch of its own; the `gp/deploy-workflow` check
  holds the other half, that no second workflow publishes.
- **Retire when:** the deploy becomes idempotent against a second publisher.
```
```entry gp-site-config
## 2026-09-18 · born · Rebuild github-pages as a nightly release task over one deploy workflow (#2101)
- **Source:** `static-website`'s `sw/site-config`, which held the same config from #611; the config
  and its check stay with the pack that builds and publishes.
- **Reason:** the publish set is deliberately additive, and the check makes the cost of that choice
  survivable. Additive inverts the failure: a forgotten entry is a missing page, and the check
  catches a path that matches nothing tracked, a tooling directory in the set and a set with no
  `index.html` before any of them reaches the default branch.
- **Rejected:** publishing the repo except the tooling, which publishes every draft, note and key
  nobody thought to exclude, and publishes each new one silently the day it lands.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at high severity, relevant on either of two independent signals,
  the site config or the vendored deploy workflow: gating on the config alone would let a repo that
  vendored the workflow and never wrote its config pass silently, which is the one case this check
  exists to report.
- **Retire when:** the artifact stops being built from an explicit list.
```
```entry gp-deploy-workflow
## 2026-09-18 · born · Rebuild github-pages as a nightly release task over one deploy workflow (#2101)
- **Source:** the presence half of `static-website`'s departed `sw/release-workflows`, over the one
  workflow this pack still vendors.
- **Reason:** the deploy runs from the repo's own `.github/` because GitHub runs a Pages deploy only
  from a workflow job in the repo's own tree, never from the mount, so the pack holds the template
  and each repo hosts a managed copy. The check holds that copy present, dispatch-only and current,
  and holds every other workflow off the Pages actions, because a second publisher or a push trigger
  deploys a tree with no version cut and no park lane.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at high severity, on the same two-signal relevance gate as
  `gp/site-config`.
- **Retire when:** the vendored surface is replaced by something the member cannot hold a stale copy
  of.
```
```entry site-release
## 2026-09-18 · born · Rebuild github-pages as a nightly release task over one deploy workflow (#2101)
- **Source:** the owner, 2026-09-17: the hosting packs should have "a daily release task that will
  bump the version and release if there was any change"; the shape is `cloudflare-site`'s
  `site-release`, which already had it.
- **Reason:** a release is a version number, a push, a dispatch and a wait, and none of the four is
  a judgment call, so the work is code and the queue supplies what a push-triggered workflow could
  not: the trigger, the gate, the retry and the park lanes. The bump lands before the deploy because
  only one of the two drifts is silent: a site serving a version the repo has no record of. A
  version consumed by a release whose deploy then failed is visible in the park and costs nothing.
- **Mechanism:** a task, scheduled, due daily and gated on `unreleased-commits`, its own term
  because no built-in asks a release's question; `agent_model: none` since there is no judgment to
  make, `expected_outcome: no_code_changes` because the bump commits to the default branch rather
  than opening a pull request nobody could usefully review, and `on_interrupt: needs-human` because
  a release is a one-shot external effect a reclaimed claim must not re-run.
```
```entry-defaults
- **Reason:** `taskScheduler.dailyHour` and its siblings let a repo move the boundaries a cadence
  was measured against, which put a seam inside every day: before the anchor hour the current period
  was still yesterday's, so one run read as consumed at 03:00 and as open at 09:00. A period is now
  the UTC calendar and nothing else, and the term says out loud what it is, a rate limit on the
  scheduler's own asking rather than a claim that there is work to do. A corpus-wide decision, cited
  here.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #2182 (Closes #1995) · pack version 60920.3.
```
```entry site-release
## 2026-09-20 · policy-changed · A task cadence measures whole UTC periods, not a per-repo anchor (#2182)
- **Mechanism:** the declaration's `due:daily` precondition becomes `schedule:at-most-daily`; the
  gate on real work is still `unreleased-commits` beside it.
```

{"number":607,"title":"leaflet: convert the tile-attribution rule to a check (#600)","body":"Prose-to-checks sweep, dispatched by **issue #600**. Pack paths swept: `.claudinite/local/packs`, `packs` (never `.claudinite/shared/`). Outcome ceiling `open-pr` — **not merged, no auto-merge armed.**

## Converted (1)

| Prose | Became | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/leaflet/RULES.md` — *"Keep the tile provider's attribution — it's a licence term, not decoration. The `attribution: '… © OpenStreetMap contributors'` on the `L.tileLayer(...)` must stay even when tidying the UI."* | **`leaflet/tile-attribution`** | blocking |

The rule constrains the layer's own options object, which is a static signature in the source, so it passes the check-the-world test. Its failure mode is exactly what a post-hoc check catches and a session cannot: the credit is dropped while tidying the UI, long after the map was wired, and nothing about the running map looks wrong afterwards.

Deduped against the live catalog first — `leaflet/asset-integrity` covers only the CDN wiring; nothing covered attribution.

## Parsed, not grepped

`grep attribution` answers the wrong question: it is satisfied by the word appearing anywhere in the file and cannot say *which* tile layer is missing it. So the check reads each `L.tileLayer(` call site, walks its own argument list to the options object, and judges only that object's own top-level keys. Consequences, all deliberate:

- `L.tileLayer.wms(...)` is a different constructor and never matches.
- Options passed as a **variable** or built by a **spread** are not judged — the literal is the only form where absence is provably absence.
- A file calling `addAttribution(` (Leaflet's documented out-of-band path) is skipped whole.
- Comments are blanked, and in HTML only inline `<script>` bodies are treated as code — a Leaflet snippet in a `<pre>` or an HTML comment is not a call site. Line numbers survive because the blanking is length-preserving.

## See-it-fail

`packs-tests/leaflet/tile-attribution.test.mjs` — 12 fixtures (4 firing, 8 quiet). Every guard was mutated and watched to bite, then restored:

| Mutation | Fixture that went red |
|---|---|
| `run()` neutered to `return []` | all 4 firing cases |
| comment/markup blanking removed | the comment-and-`<pre>`-only case |
| out-of-band `addAttribution` guard removed | the out-of-band case |
| spread tolerated instead of bailing out | the variable/spread case |
| call anchor widened past `.wms` | the `L.tileLayer.wms` case |

## Deletion test

**The prose bullet stays whole.** It carries a second rule in the same breath — *set `maxZoom` to the provider's real ceiling (OSM tops out at 19)* — a per-provider value no check can judge, and Leaflet's own default is a legitimate answer for a map that never zooms that far. The paragraph is therefore not fully covered, so it is kept whole rather than trimmed. `packs/leaflet/README.md`'s enforcement column and `packs/README.md`'s check tally (67 → 68) are updated to match.

## Green

- `node --test` over the CI test roots: **1041 pass / 0 fail** (1029 before, +12).
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: exit 0 — **0 blocking**, 9 advisory, all pre-existing `file-placement` advisories under `engine/`, untouched by this change.

{"number":2159,"title":"Add numpy-image-processing canon pack","body":"## What

A new canon pack, `packs/numpy-image-processing/`, for numeric image analysis in Python on the
NumPy + SciPy (`ndimage`) + scikit-image + Pillow stack: deriving a mask, skeleton or threshold
from an image array, and rendering the result. No existing pack homes this — `python` is generic
packaging/import prose (2 rules), and `research-project` is the process-level "iterate an
algorithm against ground truth" methodology; neither carries array-level mechanics.

## Evidence — this run's fleet sweep

Swept every covered member reachable from this session (repos whose declaration parses and names
at least one pack). Two members independently do the same kind of work — extract a mask/skeleton
from a microscopy image array and score/annotate it — on the identical library stack, and their
real source files demonstrate the same non-obvious gotchas:

- **`missingbulb/VascularColoring`** (`analysis/measure_vessels.py`) — connected-component
  filtering via `ndi.label`/`ndi.sum` fancy-indexing, neighbor-count skeleton classification via
  `ndi.convolve`, `PIL.ImageFont.truetype` wrapped in `try`/`except OSError` with an
  `ImageFont.load_default()` fallback, and `Image.NEAREST` upscaling for pixel-exact overlays.
- **`missingbulb/NoRFinder`** (`src/nor.py`, `src/harness.py`, `src/render.py`) — the
  imaged-area-only quantile (padding from `affine_transform` silently pollutes a naive statistic),
  the `>=`-vs-`>` saturation guard, `np.floor`/`np.ceil` instead of `int()` around a float center,
  the documented pull convention of `scipy.ndimage.affine_transform`, and choosing an annotation
  hue by a measured cosine-similarity margin.

Every rule in `RULES.md` traces to one of these two members' real files (cited in the pack's
`README.md`); nothing is speculative best-practice.

Also noted for the tracker (not actioned here — never a second copy of a homed pack):
`missingbulb/EdFringeNow` should declare the already-homed `python`, `web-scraping` and `leaflet`
packs (it uses all three without declaring them); `missingbulb/WIP` should declare `flutter`,
`node`, `ios` and `android`. `missingbulb/gRatio` was not swept — it carries no
`.claudinite-settings.json`, so it is not a covered member.

## Verification

- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking (fixed two: `ruleRoutingGuidance` word
  caps), advisory count unchanged net of one line-length fix in the new `RULES.md`.
- `node --test` over the CI test-root glob (`engine-tests/`, `packs/`, `vendoring/`,
  `dev/tools/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/`) — 3739 passed, 0 failed (includes the badge-tracking,
  rule-index/size-band and severity/reason-vocabulary tests the new pack's files must satisfy).
- `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` regenerated via `engine-tests/pack-directory.test.mjs`.

## Follow-up

Once merged, opening one `Adopt canon pack: numpy-image-processing` issue in each of
`VascularColoring` and `NoRFinder` — the members that evidenced it, both at `core` prominence.

{"number":1671,"title":"Promote the reviewed survivors of nine growth-promote PRs","body":"Consolidates #1021, #1157, #1204, #1345, #1372, #1409, #1451, #1524 and #1661 (all closed in favour of this one) into one reviewed change, then re-reviewed against `main` after #1711. {"number":165,"title":"Add executable-requirements pack; fill the flutter pack stub","body":"## What

Two pack changes, both earned in missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers this milestone:

**New `executable-requirements` pack** — the mechanics companion to `spec-driven-product`. Where the class playbook carries the judgment layer (doc-first, owner-owned expecteds), this pack carries the concrete framework standard so a new project or stack adopts it by convention: the `dev/requirements/` layout and shared leaf regex, `<slug>.<leaf-id>.case` naming with folder-as-kind classification, the coverage gate's full duty checklist (including manifest⇄disk equality for languages without dynamic import), the kind vocabulary, determinism rules (pinned clock, faked nondeterminism, real fonts, pixel-exact always), per-stack rendering recipes (jsdom+satori for DOM products, widget-test goldens for Flutter), the machine-managed gallery contract, and refresh-as-review-step.

It also standardizes the new **`saga` kind**: multi-step user stories rendered as ordered golden storyboards (`*.step-NN.png`) with narrative captions that surface in the spec's gallery — for requirements about *transitions and causality* ("a message sent before I arrived never appears") rather than resting states. First implementation: ShoutsAndWhispers `dev/requirements/saga/`.

**`flutter` pack: stub → earned rules** — ports-and-adapters out of the widget tree, widget-test/golden mechanics (FontManifest loading, no `pumpAndSettle` on spinners, injectable fetchers, fixed viewport, async-epoch guard), toolchain habits.

**`firebase` + `firebase-release` packs, and `android`/`ios`/`play-store-release`/`app-store-release` stubs** — Firebase rules/functions/deploy discipline; the opt-in dev/prod split standard (committed-default-dev, pipeline-injected prod config, App Check store attestation); registered stubs filled when first exercised.

**Corpus index** (`CLAUDE.md`) updated to route to the new packs.

## Verification

- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs skills/*/*.test.mjs` — 81/81 pass with the new packs present.
- `node checks/run.mjs` conformance sweep — clean (0 blocking, 0 advisory).
- Registry smoke: `loadPacks()` discovers `executable-requirements` + `firebase`; `detect` fires on the fingerprint files and not otherwise.
- Rebased onto latest `main` (linear, squash-friendly history).

Closes #180

# cloudflare-site — why its rules and checks read as they do

Maintenance and review only: the reasons behind this pack's prose and checks, for the pass that
asks whether each still earns its place. No session loads this file.

- **(check:cloudflare-site/publishes-a-site-directory)** `assets.directory` is the only boundary
  between the published site and the repo holding the vendored mount, the packs and the queue's
  workers. Widening it to the repo root publishes all of that to a public URL, and the deploy
  reports success either way. Retire the check if a Cloudflare deployment ever gains a second,
  independent statement of what is uploaded.

- **(check:cloudflare-site/version-stamp-matches-package)** The stamp is a generated copy of
  `package.json`'s version, and a copy that drifts names a build that was never served while the
  page looks perfectly normal. Retire it if the version stops being copied into the pages.

- **(check:cloudflare-site/no-second-publisher)** A workflow that deploys ships the tree with no
  version cut, no gate and no park lane; a `CNAME` file under the published tree is the previous
  host still claiming the domain. Both are leftovers rather than choices, which is why they are
  detected rather than handed to an adopter as checklist items — a checklist of steps that are
  no-ops for most adopters teaches its reader to skim it (owner, 2026-09-13: "It should not
  include turning off other registrars or disabling github pages as optional steps, so they need
  to be evaluated if they are there"). Retire it if the release ever becomes idempotent against a
  second publisher.

- **(check:cloudflare-site/beacon-token-is-not-committed)** A committed beacon token beacons from
  every checkout, fork and local preview into the production site's numbers, and the page is
  identical either way. Retire it if the loader stops taking its token from the served file.

content.content:
The minor was a bare MMDD, which runs backwards every New Year: 1231 is
followed by 0101. So "later means bigger" — the one thing every reader of a
version assumes — stopped being true once a year, and the ordering rested
entirely on the build counter beside it.

The minor now counts years from a fixed epoch before the month and day, so it
is strictly increasing with no wrap to absorb: 2026-09-17 is 10917 and
2027-01-01 is 20101. The offset simply grows, taking the minor to six digits in
2035, which is still numerically above 2034's five — asserted, because that is
the point at which a scheme with a single year digit would have had to wrap.

Existing adopters cross over safely without anything to migrate: the old minor
was at most four digits (1231) and the new one is at least five (10101), so
every repo's next release sorts above its last whatever date it lands on.

The name `patch` went with it — `build` is what the field has always been, a
counter that advances per release rather than per fix.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.content:
commit 9750ab1e1a38e5dad698401f3091f3a212ea3697
Author: missingbulb <73882448+missingbulb@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Fri Sep 18 08:59:14 2026 +0300

    Split the website packs by ownership: public-website, github-pages, cloudflare-site (#2101)
    
    * Split the GitHub Pages half of static-website into a github-pages pack
    
    static-website conflated two things: what is true of a static site (a version
    scheme, an explicit publish set, a config file, a PR gate) and what is true of
    one served from GitHub Pages (release on push, the Release it cuts, the Pages
    deploy, the subpath it is served from). A repo hosting its site anywhere else
    could take only half the pack, and the half it left behind was where three of
    the four checks lived.
    
    The serving half is now its own pack. github-pages holds the orchestrator and
    the three reusable workflows (renamed github-pages-*), the gp/pages-workflows
    check, the subpath rule, the releasing-to-github-pages skill, its own standing
    vendoring record, and the one-time repository settings as adoptionHandover.
    It requires static-website, whose composite actions its workflows still run.
    
    static-website keeps the version scheme, site.config, the publish set, the
    three actions and the PR gate. Its checks can no longer gate on an orchestrator
    that has left the pack, so relevance moves to adoptedStandard: the site config
    OR the vendored CI gate, either sufficient — two independent signals, because
    the missing config is itself the thing sw/site-config exists to report. The
    presence half of the departed sw/release-workflows becomes sw/vendored-pipeline
    over the files the pack still owns.
    
    The pack has no adopters since EdFringeNow removed it, so nothing is migrated
    and no legacy spelling is carried. Open question 1 of docs/website-release-flows
    is answered against D1 and recorded there.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Put sw/version-scheme on the same relevance gate as its three siblings
    
    The README claimed relevance for all four checks was adoptedStandard, but
    version-scheme still opened on its own read of site.config — the same
    inconsistency this split exists to remove, reintroduced one file down.
    
    No behaviour changes: a missing config already short-circuited the rule, and
    still does on the line below the gate, which now says out loud that
    sw/site-config owns that case. What changes is that the four rules read alike
    and the README's claim about them is true.
    
    CONFIG_PATH now comes from vendored-pipeline, its one definition, rather than
    through a re-export site-config.mjs was only carrying for other modules.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Leave the website-release-flows design doc alone
    
    A DESIGN.md carries the end state and its rationale — never progress, a
    superseded-decision narrative or an owner attribution, which is what the
    state note I added was made of. The record that the split answers its open
    question 1 against D1 belongs in the pull request, where it already is.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Name the Pages skill for what it does, and cut it to the actions
    
    It does not perform a release — it wires, changes and debugs the vendored
    pipeline that does, so it is github-pages-pipeline now and its description
    says which moments want it.
    
    Halved: the stage-by-stage narrative of the publish reusable is that file's
    own header comment, and what the pack does and does not own is the README's.
    What is left is the three steps that wire a repo, a table of the four things
    anyone actually drives it to do, and the two facts that surprise people — the
    pipeline writes no version of its own, and a GITHUB_TOKEN push fires no
    workflow.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Cut both packs' rules to the ration, evidence into references.md
    
    Every rule ran 150-200 words where the format asks for one sentence near 40,
    and several opened on a state of the world ("A published file is a file the
    publish set names") rather than on the act that brings a reader to them.
    
    Each is now keyed to what the reader is doing — adding a file the site serves,
    changing the publish set, deciding a cache lifetime — and carries only the
    consequence needed to apply it under pressure. Nothing is weakened and nothing
    is strengthened: the rationale moves to each pack's new references.md, which
    no session loads and which exists so a later pass can reaffirm or retire a
    rule from its recorded reason. The evidence goes with it, the 0-bytes-of-3.1MB
    timezone rewrite and the join check that passed at 6% included.
    
    One rule's subject pointed back at its neighbour with a "that", so it read as
    a clause rather than a situation; it stands alone now.
    
    Five of static-website's rules are rewritten in place and one is genuinely
    retired — the subpath rule, which moved to github-pages with the split. That
    is what rules-append-only reports on this change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019JVtPHEVd2btsZ522qWQJA
    
    * Publish the workflow-run and Pages reads a release worker needs
    
    A worker that dispatches a workflow gets a 204 and no run id, so it
    finds its run as the workflow's newest dispatch and polls it; and a
    Pages release probes the site at the URL the Pages API names. Three

## PR #827 · 2026-08-14 · Declared checks are JSON, one file per pack
- by @missingbulb · model Claude · refs #826 · pack version 2
- google-token-audience-pinned (born), google-token-email-verified (born)

> * Declared checks: one file per pack, not one file per rule
>
> The 25 pattern-rule declarations from the four conversion rounds were 25
> modules of ~17 lines each, all data. A declaration is a table row, not a
> module: reading a pack's declared surface meant opening five files, the
> shared constants were re-imported per rule, and each manifest carried an
> import line and a list entry per declaration.
>
> Each pack now keeps its declarations in one declared-checks.mjs — a named
> export per rule (so the tests still import one directly), default export
> the array the manifest spreads into its rule list. The three skills inline
> their declarations into the checks.mjs array they already had. Rules with a
> hand-written run(ctx) stay their own modules.
>
> Nothing behavioural moves: `--list` is byte-identical against main (88
> rules), the world sweep finds the same 0 blocking / 28 advisory, and the
> 1607-test suite passes with only import lines changed.
>
> * Declared checks are JSON: no comments, no doc pointer, failureMessage
>
> Owner review on #827: the file that holds only declarations should not be
> code. A pack's declarations are now the array in
> packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json (a skill's in its own beside checks.mjs),
> discovered structurally by the pack registry and compiled by the pattern
> engine — no import, no manifest line; writing the declaration adds the check.
>
> The format drops what the declaration was borrowing from prose. No comments
> (JSON cannot hold one, so the no-comments rule is enforced by construction),
> no `description` and no `doc` pointer — a declaration states its own case —
> and `why` is renamed `failureMessage` for what it is: the line the agent
> reads when the check fires. Regexes are strings in /pattern/flags form,
> compiled at load; a path-or-pattern key still reads a plain string as an
> exact path, and a plain string anywhere else is reported with the key that
> got it.
>
> The registry reaches the compiler lazily, only where a declaration file
> exists, so a tree carrying just the pack machinery loads as before. Both

```entry _pack
  everywhere. Adoption stays a moment a person is present, because it wires two workflow files and
  the routine endpoints a member cannot converge into place.
```

```entry tasks-usage-fold
  long an occurrence took to travel from a tick to a converged item. It is the machinery's own
  past-data plane, kept beside the session fold's rather than inside it. Every tier is appended
  once, because every source is a watermarked REST listing rather than a file re-read for free, so
  a counting fix applies forward only; the week tier drops the per-run map, whose keys would grow
  the file a row a week with nothing pruning it. Where the pack config carries no Actions minute
  rate there is no spend key anywhere, never a zero, and the rate a file was priced at is written
  beside the numbers so a later rate cannot silently re-price frozen rows.

  lane, gated on a precondition reading the fold's own watermark against the scheduler's most
  recent anchor - the mark's own movement, and no API call, which matters on a term asked at every
  tick. No built-in movement term can see the machinery: they all read the project's commits,
  issues, pull requests and captures, and a repo whose only activity is its own queue is silent by
  all four.
```

1. **Review document** — `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md`: measured census and sweep timings, vocabulary and message analysis, per-rule conversion audit, framework survey (adopt idioms, adopt no tool).
2. **Vocabulary facilities** — `scanFileClasses`/`excludeFileClasses` (shared named file sets), structural self-exclusion of a skill's own content, rule-level `fix` default, `scanIgnoringComments` (string-aware), and full spec-key validation so a typo'd key throws instead of silently asserting nothing.
3. **jwt conversion** — the five jwt rules become two `declared-checks.json` files; the rule modules, both `checks.mjs` and the pack's `scan.mjs` are deleted (~160 net lines out), tests exercise the declared rules through the same fixtures.
4. **Perf** — the barrier scan gets a precomputed completion index + per-context shared scan state (274ms → ~180ms, findings byte-identical), and the base-ref refresh gains a 5-minute per-ref freshness window (1.21s → 0.53s back-to-back; the Stop hook no longer pays the fetch every turn).
5. **Key merges** — `checkParsedFile`/`forEachParsedEntry`/`equalParsedValues` → one select-then-assert `checkParsedFiles`; `listedInFile`/`coveredByGlobLine` → `requireIndexCoverage` with the divergent absence/anchoring semantics declared per entry. Legacy spellings stay accepted (member local packs may carry them; a rename has no fleet carrier) and normalize at load.
6. **Message discipline** — a blocking `declared-check-messages` meta-check (32-word cap per field, no fix repeated within a rule), authored red-first (17 findings), and the rewrite that turns it green. Tally recomputed 89 → 90; the stale basics row corrected.
7. **Barriers rephrase** — the scan engine moves to `engine/checks/helpers/reference-scanning.mjs`; the vocabulary gains `forbidReferences`; the three fixed barriers (claudinite-isolation, product-wiki-isolation, pack-independence) become declared checks in their owning packs, byte-identical findings on the home (minus the `doc` field declared checks drop). The per-repo config rule and the `contributes` seam keep working on the moved engine.

**Consumer safety**: two new rehearsal fixtures/changes — a member whose local pack declares checks in a legacy spelling converges green under the new blocking meta-check; the consumer-safe-change guard was satisfied by fixture (additive change), not record. At merge time, the standing verify-through-a-member rule applies: force a fleet baseline and confirm one member's converge before calling it shipped.

Verification: 1668/1668 tests, world sweep 0 blocking, work sweep clean, barrier-family findings diffed byte-identical against the pre-change baseline.

{"number":350,"title":"google-identity: convert the three prose rules into skill-owned check-the-work rules","body":"Converts the `google-identity` pack's three prose rules (PR #-pending on this branch, commit 1b64b32) into deterministic checks, per the owner's direction: keep the pack, add a skill for the activity, move the rules into check-the-work tests, and delete all the prose.

## What changed

**The pack stays, prose-free.** `packs/google-identity/RULES.md` is deleted; `pack.mjs` drops `prose` and now mounts the new skill (`skills: ['google-id-token-validation']`), keeping the pack as the hand-declared anchor (`detect: null` unchanged).

**New skill `google-id-token-validation`** — a minimal SKILL.md (the trigger plus the three rule ids; no re-teaching, so nothing to drift) and a `checks.mjs` owning three rules, discovered by `skills/registry.mjs` and run at every Stop and in CI. The failure message is the instruction:

| Rule | Severity | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `google-token-audience-pinned` | blocking | a config-format file (yaml/json/toml/tf) declaring the bare Google accounts issuer with no — or an explicitly empty — expected audience |
| `google-client-id-single-origin` | advisory | the same `…apps.googleusercontent.com` literal hardcoded in ≥2 files (a smell to judge: separate deploy units legitimately hold one copy each) |
| `google-token-email-verified` | blocking | handler code reading the `email` claim with no `email_verified` check, or strict-boolean-comparing `email_verified` behind an API Gateway authorizer (which stringifies claims) |

**Relevance gates** (a skill check runs on every repo): rule 1 scopes to config formats bearing the bare issuer origin — the path-form client OAuth URLs never match; rule 3 gates per-file on a verified-claims context and per-repo on a Google-identity marker, and skips test files; all three exclude the skill's own directory so its fixtures never flag the corpus repo. Code-form verifiers (jose/google-auth-library defaults) have no reliable file-scoped signature and are documented out of rule 1's scope.

**Answering "are you sure they weren't checkable?"** — the original commit was too conservative. There is no *universal* signature, but file-scoped signatures cover the grounded cases (the TLDR provenance is exactly rule 1's authorizer-config shape), so the rules convert; the signature-less residue (hand-rolled verifier code) is what the checks' comments document as out of scope.

## Tests

13 new fixture tests (scratch-repo harness), each rule proven both directions — violating fixtures find, clean ones (path-form OAuth URLs, per-deploy-unit copies, string-compared `email_verified`, marker-less repos, test files) stay quiet — and mutation-tested red (neutering `run()` fails exactly the violating-fixture tests). Full suite: 341 pass. Whole-repo sweep: clean (one new `file-placement` acceptance for the engine-lib import, mirroring the `unattended-agents` precedent).

Catalogs updated (`packs/README.md` row, `skills/README.md` entry) to satisfy `catalog-completeness`; the pack's `skills` list satisfies `skill-ownership`.

Refs #303

```entry _pack
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Reason:** a repo serving a static tree from Cloudflare Workers static assets on its own domain
  now gets the whole deployment from the canon rather than from the one repo that had built it: the
  nightly release, the boundary of what reaches a public URL, and the parts of the deployment only
  a person holding the Cloudflare account can do. The pack asks its adopters nothing, because
  everything it needs about a deployment (the published tree, the hostnames claimed, whether
  analytics is wanted) is already stated structurally in the repo's own wrangler config and in
  whether a published file carries the beacon placeholder, and a question whose answer is already
  in the tree is a second place for it to be wrong.
- **Mechanism:** the pack manifest, fingerprinted by a near-root JSON wrangler config that declares
  `assets.directory`. The sibling `cloudflare-workers` pack fingerprints on a wrangler config of
  any shape because it is about the runtime and its bindings; a config declaring a published
  directory is a site, so a Worker backend with no assets carries none of this.
```

```entry releasing-a-cloudflare-site
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Reason:** forcing a release, rolling one back, reading a park and knowing what only a person
  can change is operating knowledge wanted at one moment, not in every session; the four properties
  a change to the release must preserve are what a session editing it needs before it edits.
- **Mechanism:** a skill, forced onto any edit of a wrangler config or the release task, so the
  guard holds the edit until it is loaded.
```

```entry site-release
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Reason:** the release is a work item because the queue owns its trigger, its gate, its secrets
  and its park lanes. It preflights every claimed hostname in public DNS before it consumes a
  version number and parks `needs-human-action` naming the record it found, an inherited `CNAME` or
  a GitHub Pages apex address, so the previous host's leftovers are evaluated rather than handed to
  an adopter as checklist items; an unreachable resolver is inconclusive, never a verdict. The bump
  lands before the upload because of the two possible drifts only one is invisible, a site serving
  a version the repo has no record of.
- **Mechanism:** a task, scheduled daily and gated on the branch having moved past the last release
  commit, read off the `Claudinite-Task:` trailer, with `on_interrupt: needs-human` and the two
  Cloudflare secrets declared so a missing one parks at the task's own gate before anything is
  touched.
```
```entry cloudflare-site-publishes-a-site-directory
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Reason:** `assets.directory` is the only boundary between the published site and the repo
  holding the vendored mount, the packs and the queue's workers. Widening it to the repo root
  publishes all of that to a public URL, and the deploy reports success either way.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at critical severity, on the wrangler config the pack
  fingerprints on.
- **Retire when:** a Cloudflare deployment gains a second, independent statement of what is
  uploaded.
```
```entry cloudflare-site-no-second-publisher
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Source:** the owner, 2026-09-13: adoption "should not include turning off other registrars or
  disabling github pages as optional steps, so they need to be evaluated if they are there".
- **Reason:** a workflow that deploys ships the tree with no version cut, no gate and no park lane;
  a `CNAME` file under the published tree is the previous host still claiming the domain. Both are
  leftovers rather than choices.
- **Rejected:** listing them as adoption steps. A checklist of steps that are no-ops for most
  adopters teaches its reader to skim the list that exists to stop them skimming.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at high severity, over the repo's workflows and the published
  tree.
- **Retire when:** the release becomes idempotent against a second publisher.
```
```entry cloudflare-site-beacon-token-is-not-committed
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Reason:** a committed beacon token beacons from every checkout, fork and local preview into the
  production site's numbers, and the page is identical either way. The matcher strips a script's
  comments first, so a commented-out loader, which beacons nothing, does not read as a committed
  token.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at high severity, filed under legal rather than correctness.
- **Retire when:** the loader stops taking its token from the served file.
```

```entry _pack
## 2026-09-17 · reworded · cloudflare-site: put a year offset in the release version's date (#2100)
- **Reason:** the minor was a bare `MMDD`, which runs backwards every New Year, `1231` followed by
  `0101`, so "later means bigger" stopped being true once a year and the ordering rested entirely
  on the build counter beside it. The minor now counts years from a fixed epoch before the month
  and day, strictly increasing with no wrap to absorb. Existing adopters cross over with nothing to
  migrate: the old minor was at most four digits and the new one at least five, so every repo's
  next release sorts above its last whatever date it lands on. `patch` became `build`, which is
  what the field had always been, a counter that advances per release rather than per fix.
```
```entry-defaults
- **Source:** the owner's boundary, 2026-09-17: a hosting pack "needs to only care itself with how
  to serve, wire release, maintain a release ... not anything else that deals 'being a website'
  like versions".
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Fable 5.1, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #2101 · pack version 60918.1.
```
```entry _pack
## 2026-09-18 · split · Move versioning out of cloudflare-site into public-website's seam (#2101)
- **Reason:** the version, the page stamp and the drift check are not facts about Cloudflare, so
  they leave for `public-website` and the release reaches them through that pack's
  `public/version.mjs` when it is declared, skipping them when it is not. The release keeps its
  shape, the bump before the upload and the bump commit as the gate's high-water mark. A migration
  record declares `public-website` on every member serving from Cloudflare so an adopter keeps its
  versioning without a hand edit, and the old bump path stays as a delegating shim because a
  member's own prose may still run it, its retirement filed as #2113. The pack also stops naming
  `github-pages`: a hosting pack knows no other host.
- **Mechanism:** the manifest keeps the serving half only; `bump-version.mjs` becomes a shim and
  the `version-stamp-matches-package` check leaves with the scheme.
```
```entry publishing-site-anywhere
## 2026-09-18 · reworded · Move versioning out of cloudflare-site into public-website's seam (#2101)
- **Reason:** the task no longer cuts the version, it advances one that `public-website` owns, and
  with that pack undeclared it cuts nothing at all, so the rule says "advances".
```
```entry releasing-a-cloudflare-site
## 2026-09-18 · reworded · Move versioning out of cloudflare-site into public-website's seam (#2101)
- **Reason:** the first of the four properties a change must preserve now reads through
  `public-website`'s seam rather than off `package.json` directly, and says what happens with that
  pack undeclared: the site is uploaded unversioned and the run says so. The `decision` park lane's
  example follows.
```
```entry-defaults
- **Reason:** `taskScheduler.dailyHour` and its siblings let a repo move the boundaries a cadence
  was measured against, which put a seam inside every day: before the anchor hour the current period
  was still yesterday's, so one run read as consumed at 03:00 and as open at 09:00. A period is now
  the UTC calendar and nothing else, and the term says out loud what it is, a rate limit on the
  scheduler's own asking rather than a claim that there is work to do. A corpus-wide decision, cited
  here.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #2182 (Closes #1995) · pack version 60920.3.
```
```entry site-release
## 2026-09-20 · policy-changed · A task cadence measures whole UTC periods, not a per-repo anchor (#2182)
- **Mechanism:** the declaration's `due:daily` precondition becomes `schedule:at-most-daily`; the
  gate on real work is still `unreleased-commits` beside it.
```

```entry cloudflare-site-no-second-publisher
- **Source:** the owner, 2026-09-13: adoption "should not include turning off other registrars or
  disabling github pages as optional steps, so they need to be evaluated if they are there".
- **Reason:** a workflow that deploys ships the tree with no version cut, no gate and no park lane;
  a `CNAME` file under the published tree is the previous host still claiming the domain. Both are
  leftovers rather than choices.
- **Rejected:** listing them as adoption steps. A checklist of steps that are no-ops for most
  adopters teaches its reader to skim the list that exists to stop them skimming.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at high severity, over the repo's workflows and the published
  tree.
- **Retire when:** the release becomes idempotent against a second publisher.
```
```entry cloudflare-site-beacon-token-is-not-committed
## 2026-09-13 · born · Add the cloudflare-site pack: serving a static site from Cloudflare (#1982)
- **Reason:** a committed beacon token beacons from every checkout, fork and local preview into the
  production site's numbers, and the page is identical either way. The matcher strips a script's
  comments first, so a commented-out loader, which beacons nothing, does not read as a committed
  token.
- **Mechanism:** a check, blocking at high severity, filed under legal rather than correctness.
- **Retire when:** the loader stops taking its token from the served file.
```

```entry _pack
## 2026-09-17 · reworded · cloudflare-site: put a year offset in the release version's date (#2100)
- **Reason:** the minor was a bare `MMDD`, which runs backwards every New Year, `1231` followed by
  `0101`, so "later means bigger" stopped being true once a year and the ordering rested entirely
  on the build counter beside it. The minor now counts years from a fixed epoch before the month
  and day, strictly increasing with no wrap to absorb. Existing adopters cross over with nothing to
  migrate: the old minor was at most four digits and the new one at least five, so every repo's
  next release sorts above its last whatever date it lands on. `patch` became `build`, which is
  what the field had always been, a counter that advances per release rather than per fix.
```

```entry _pack
  they leave for `public-website` and the release reaches them through that pack's
```

```entry _pack
## 2026-07-19 · born · google-identity: prose to skill-owned checks (#350)
- **Reason:** the extension-client half of Google auth was already homed in the chrome-extension pack, and the server side - the validator that accepts the token - was unhomed.
- **Mechanism:** the pack manifest, declared by hand with no fingerprint: the technology shows up as the Google accounts OIDC issuer inside a JWT-authorizer or verifier config, which has no canonical filename and co-occurs with other stacks, so an absent `detect` skips the drift check in both directions and declaring the pack is authoritative.
```
```entry google-id-token-validation
## 2026-07-19 · born · google-identity: prose to skill-owned checks (#350)
- **Reason:** the pack opened with three prose rules judged to have no reliable check signature. The owner's direction reversed that in the same pull request: there is no universal signature, but file-scoped ones cover every grounded case, so the rules became checks, the prose was deleted and the pack kept only as the hand-declared anchor. The signature-less residue - a hand-rolled verifier in code - is documented as out of the checks' scope.
- **Mechanism:** the skill, mounted by the pack and reached by its description, carrying the activity and nothing about its own enforcement: the checks run on their own at every Stop and in CI and each failure message carries its rule, so a skill listing their ids would duplicate the mechanism and drift from it.
```
```entry google-token-audience-pinned
## 2026-07-19 · born · google-identity: prose to skill-owned checks (#350)
- **Reason:** a Google ID token is accepted on signature, issuer and audience, and every Google-issued token shares the one issuer - so a validator whose expected audience is unset accepts a token minted for any Google OAuth client, an authentication bypass that looks entirely valid. Judged on repo state on purpose: an unset audience already merged is a live bypass and must keep firing until it is fixed.
- **Mechanism:** a blocking check of the skill, gated to config-format files that use the word issuer and carry the bare Google accounts origin - a path form is a client-side OAuth URL rather than an issuer - since a skill's check runs on every repo.
```
```entry google-token-email-verified
## 2026-07-19 · born · google-identity: prose to skill-owned checks (#350)
- **Reason:** a Google ID token carries `email` whether or not Google verified it, so an action gated on the bare claim trusts an unverified address; and behind an API Gateway authorizer the claim arrives as a string, so a strict boolean comparison silently rejects every genuinely verified user.
- **Mechanism:** a blocking check of the skill, gated per file on a verified-claims context and per repo on a Google-identity marker, test files excluded.
```

> WHY A PACK AND NOT ENGINE CODE. The dashboard is not part of running the scheduler:
> nothing converges, scheduler runs or executes because it exists, and a member that never
> looks at it should not carry it. Engine code is what every member runs; this is
> content a member OPTS INTO, and adoptable content in this corpus is a pack. That
> also buys it the things a pack has and engine code does not — its own version and
> migration lane, a declaration that gates it, and an adoption moment at which its
> deployment can be wired.
>
> WHAT IT READS. Only the queue's own vocabulary and the task declarations at HEAD,
> through the tasks pack's published `public/`, so the page cannot drift from the
> mechanism it renders. Those relative paths resolve identically in the canon (`packs/<id>/`
> beside its siblings) and in a member's mount (`.claudinite/shared/packs/<id>/`), which is
> why the pack can be read straight out of the mount with nothing rewritten.
>
> NO PROSE. There is no way to write the dashboard wrongly in a consuming repo — it is
> a page, not a practice — and prose here would cost every session in every declaring
> repo tokens for something no session acts on. Its README carries the explanation
> instead and `prose` stays null.
>
> PACKS CONTRIBUTE TO THIS PAGE, as data and never as code. A pack ships a descriptor
> (`packs/<id>/dashboard.json`, found by path convention — nothing registers it) naming
> what it has to say; its values come either from its own generated file in the
> member's tree or from one of the two platform facts the page already reads for every
> member. `descriptor-usable`, this pack's one check, holds a descriptor to what the
> page's OWN reader accepts, which the JSON Schema beside it structurally cannot,
> because the failure is silent — a rejected descriptor renders as one apologetic line
> in someone else's browser and nothing goes red where the author is looking.
>
> PUBLISHING IS A TASK, AND A FOUR-STEP WORKFLOW. `.github/workflows/` is the one
> directory the nightly update can never push to (the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is
> refused there), so whatever the deploy keeps there is frozen at adoption. It keeps
> the least it can: a Pages deploy with source "GitHub Actions" is marketplace actions
> that only workflow YAML can invoke, so the seeded workflow (`seedOps`, below) holds
> exactly those — checkout of `gh-pages`, configure, upload, deploy — and nothing that
> could ever need to change. The `publish-pages` task owns the rest: when to run, the
> build, the push of the built tree to `gh-pages`, the dispatch, the follow-through.
> What adoption cannot do is enable Pages — the handover step below.

- That reads fine until a fleet deployment loses its roster source — a dropped key, a renamed artifact, an enumeration that was never configured — and publishes a one-repo dashboard that looks entirely intentional.
- The [publish-pages task](tasks/publish-pages/README.md) builds the site whenever the page's sources move and fires [the deploy workflow](stubs/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml) adoption seeds into `.github/workflows/` — four `uses:` steps and nothing else — and **you must enable Pages with source *GitHub Actions***, a repository setting no Action can flip; until then that task parks naming it, and nothing else is affected.
- **The page is gated on a credential**, on a screen of its own that is all a viewer sees until they have one.
- The paste box that used to stand there asked every viewer to go and mint a PAT, which is worse than the thing sign-in replaced, and it was what a deployment shipped with by default.
- The credential dies with the tab unless the viewer ticks **Remember me**, which keeps it in this browser (`localStorage`) until they sign out.
- Only members of the organization that owns it can authorize it" — a stranger cannot even sign in; - making it public lets anyone authorize it, but a user access token "can only access resources that both the user and app can access", so until they install that App on their own account every member row still reads *not visible to you*; - and if they did install it, their redirect URI would have to live in someone else's App and their tokens would be minted by someone else's endpoint.
- So an adopter with no app of their own registers one — the checklist below — and a dashboard is not readable until they have.
- Ninety daily points across a table column is a sawtooth of weekends and Tuesdays, and a sawtooth has no shape to read — which is the whole reason the column exists rather than the single date it replaced.
- The rung that matters is `scarce`: the staleness floor reaches the **reset**, so a full page refresh costs nothing until the window rolls.
- The build is inert until the mount carries the pack (adopted, not yet converged): it exits clean with no `_site`, and the workflow skips the deploy rather than replacing a working site with an empty artifact.

> It becomes DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET; no deployment can be carrying the
> old name, so there is nothing to migrate.

> The declaration contract now rejects both names no secret may take: the
> GITHUB_ prefix, and CLAUDINITE_*, which belongs to the code-work variables
> and which task-code-work-env reads as a variable nobody sets.
