    Move the environment setup script into the web pack, and converge the clone's git config at session start (#956)
    
    * Converge the clone's git config at session start, not in the pasted setup script
    
    The environment Setup script configured `merge.ours.driver` and `rerere.enabled`
    on the repo. That is per-clone state set once at image-build time and only where
    someone pasted the script, so a terminal clone never had it and a re-cloned
    checkout lost it. It moves to the SessionStart orchestrator as a fail-soft
    `git-config` step beside the other converge work, where the vendored mount
    carries it fleet-wide with no re-paste.
    
    What is left in the setup script is the one thing only an environment image can
    do — the active packs' declared installs — with the header cut to how to use it;
    the legacy fetch-mount caveat went away with the vendoring flip, and the
    mechanism prose lives in bootstrap.md Part 9.
    
    Refs #955
    
    * Move the environment setup script into the web pack
    
    Pasting a body into an environment's Setup script field is a capability of the
    managed container a web session runs in, not engine machinery: the engine's part
    is aggregating the active packs' `env` declarations, which stays in
    env-requirements.mjs. The script moves to
    packs/claude-code-web-users-support/, is described in that pack's README and
    charter, and gets one short rule saying to paste it whole.
    
    Core stops naming it, per the barriers graph: bootstrap.md Part 9 routes through
    packs/README.md, and the session-start alert tells the reader to locate the
    script by name in their own mount rather than spelling a pack path from engine
    code.
    
    Refs #955
    
    * Refresh the packs catalog row and prose tally after the rebase
    
    The web pack now carries a fourth rule (the Setup script body), and main
    gained a pack in the meantime.
    
    Refs #955

The remedy that works: truncate that file to empty FIRST (`: > packs/<pack>/provenance/<element>.md`), then apply the element's full derived history in date order, the conversion's own entry read as evidence and its `Reason`/`Retire when` moved onto the entries they actually evidence. This is the rewrite `changing-pack-elements` sanctions — "the backfill replacing what the conversion wrote with the element's derived history, once" — so it is in bounds, but do it deliberately: read the conversion entry before you truncate, and make sure nothing it carried is dropped rather than relocated. Expect a `provenance-change-recorded` advisory per rewritten file from `check_the_work.mjs` afterwards; that is the case its own fix text sanctions, so leave it and say so in the PR body.

input.body:
Backfills every empty provenance file in three packs, and trims the README and manifest header of the history the entries now carry. It advances #2169 and closes nothing.

## What the history turned out to be

**`executable-requirements`** (14 files). The pack is one origin plus five decisions. #165 opened it with the whole framework standard, distilled from three fleet projects whose facets the pull request splits: GoogleCalendarEventCreator (the origin, jsdom rendering), TLDR (the cross-tier `server` kind) and ShoutsAndWhispers (the Flutter port and the first `saga`). That split is on the entries it belongs to - the shared attribution on the commit's defaults, ShoutsAndWhispers on `write-a-saga` and `flutter-rule`, GoogleCalendarEventCreator on `browser-extension-dom`, whose "no real browser" clause is a genuine `Rejected`. #206 added the animated APNG saga golden (GIF rejected: its palette and dithering are not deterministic). #311 bore `feature-requirements-first` on the new conversation surface, and #338 widened its gate after a finding no commit could clear in CrosswordChat. #401 gave the pack its adoption interview and added the one-liner and kind-selection conventions. #1060 stopped the prose naming its neighbours, #1634 stripped the descriptive framing from `RULES.md`, and #1667 moved the leaf, saga and determinism rules into the three path-forced skills - the ten elements that arrived there are written as `born` in #165 where the lesson actually entered the pack and `moved` in #1667, rather than born at the extraction.

**`leaflet`** (7 files, plus a new `_declined.md`). All five rules were born together in #403, a weekly pack-discovery run against EdFringeNow, each grounded in a named file of that site. #467 cut the "Grounded in" notes and the consequence prose; #1575 recovered the two rules' rationale and re-confirmed the notes stay cut (#1571) - both recorded, with the recovered rationale on the `born` entries it evidences. Two rules later converted: the CDN pin and SRI rule at #510, and the tile-attribution rule at #607, which #510 had weighed and left as prose until the out-of-band `addAttribution` guard made a confident detection possible; both conversions carry their deletion-test verdict and what grepping would have got wrong. #510 also declined the other three as checks (runtime and layout-intent behaviours with no artifact signature) - that is the new `_declined.md`.

**`google-identity`** (4 files). One pull request, #350, carries the whole pack: born from TLDR's API Gateway JWT authorizer to home the validator side of Google auth (the client side was already homed), opened as three prose rules and converted to skill-owned checks inside the same pull request when the owner's direction reversed the "no reliable signature" judgment - there is no universal signature, but file-scoped ones cover every grounded case. The skill's entry records why it names none of its own rule ids. #839 then moved both checks' gates onto shared file classes and the engine's structural self-exclusion, and #1060 took the neighbour pack out of the README and the skill.

## Corrections to the brief's derivation

- **`Closes` vs `Refs`.** The brief derives `Landed` from the commit trailer; the pull request bodies are authoritative and disagree four times - #165 closes #180, #311 fixes #310 and closes #314, #1667 closes #1662 (GitHub also lists it as the closer), #1634 closes #1632.
- **A version row the brief calls unclaimed.** `60902.1` is listed under "version rows no commit here claims" for both `executable-requirements` and `leaflet`. `git show aaa7938b -- packs/<pack>/VERSIONS.md` shows #1634 adding that row in both packs; the entries name it.
- **`marker-needs-css` drafted as born in #467.** `git show b5103ea4:packs/leaflet/RULES.md` has the rule in full at #403; #467 only shortened its trigger sentence, which is what the brief matches on. Written as born in #403.
- **The two checks drafted as born in #827.** `google-token-audience-pinned` and `google-token-email-verified` were born in #350 as coded rules; #790 re-expressed them as declarations and #827 moved those to JSON, neither changing what they demand. Written as born in #350.
- **`feature-requirements-first` at #338 drafted `reworded`.** It changed the check's gate (resolve `config.spec`, self-skip when the spec is absent), so it is `severity-changed`.
- **The ten `#1667` elements drafted as born there.** Their text is in `RULES.md` from #165; `moved` is the honest kind, with `born` back-dated to where the lesson entered.

## Trimmed files

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/executable-requirements/README.md` | 4267 | 3605 |
| `packs/executable-requirements/pack.mjs` | 2463 | 1830 |
| `packs/leaflet/README.md` | 1332 | 897 |
| `packs/leaflet/pack.mjs` | 1554 | 1025 |
| `packs/google-identity/README.md` | 1050 | 901 |
| `packs/google-identity/pack.mjs` | 1332 | 771 |

What moved: the "Distilled from" paragraphs and the `Provenance:` lines (now `Source` on each `_pack` born entry), the manifests' why-it-fingerprints-so and why-it-is-prose-free reasoning, the adoption interview's rationale, and the two duplicated mechanism sentences.

## Verification

- `provenance.mjs check` on each pack: the full file-to-carrier listing, no fault, exit 0.
- Full offline suite, 322 test files: **3808 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world`: exit 0, 0 blocking, 47 advisory - all pre-existing, and none naming these three packs (each has left the `provenance-integrity` list).
- `check_the_work`: exit 0, 0 blocking, 2 advisory - `provenance-change-recorded` on `leaflet/provenance/default-embedded-mid.md` and `keep-tile-providers.md`, the two files the references conversion had filled. That is the one rewrite the skill sanctions ("the backfill replacing what the conversion wrote"), which the check's own fix text names; the conversion's `Reason` and `Retire when` are preserved on the `born` entries they evidence.
- `git status --porcelain`: only `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` under the three packs.

No carrier changed, and no version was bumped.

One gap to note: `google-client-id-single-origin`, the third check of the `google-id-token-validation` skill, has no provenance file - the marking pass does not name a skill's coded check module, so `provenance.mjs check` reports no fault for it and this run had nothing to append to.

Remedy for a wall you may hit on the references.md-converted files: `apply` refuses an entry dated before the file's last one, so you cannot append an honest `born` at the element's real birth to a file whose conversion `born` is dated 2026-09-14.

The remedy that works: truncate that file to empty FIRST (`: > packs/<pack>/provenance/<element>.md`), then apply the element's full derived history in date order, the conversion's own entry read as evidence and its `Reason`/`Retire when` moved onto the entries they actually evidence. This is the rewrite `changing-pack-elements` sanctions — "the backfill replacing what the conversion wrote with the element's derived history, once" — so it is in bounds, but do it deliberately: read the conversion entry before you truncate, and make sure nothing it carried is dropped rather than relocated. Expect a `provenance-change-recorded` advisory per rewritten file from `check_the_work.mjs` afterwards; that is the case its own fix text sanctions, so leave it and say so in the PR body.

Four things two completed runs of this same task found, in case they save you time:

1. `Landed` was wrong about `Closes` vs `Refs` on every older PR both runs checked — fourteen out of fourteen. Read every body.
2. Several `born` drafts sat on the wrong commit, because the brief names an element by the file carrying it TODAY. A check converted from a coded module to a declaration, or a rule that was a prose section before it became a bullet, drafts as `born` at the conversion. Prove the real birth with `git show '<sha>^:<old path>'`.
3. Every version row the brief listed as unclaimed turned out to be claimed — `git log -S'<row text>'` finds the commit that wrote it.
4. An evidence or member table in a README is history too, even though the brief's "README sections" list excludes tables by design. And when you trim a README, re-read whatever pointed at the sentence you removed: one run found an "above" cross-reference left dangling.

{"number":165,"title":"Add executable-requirements pack; fill the flutter pack stub","body":"## What

Two pack changes, both earned in missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers this milestone:

**New `executable-requirements` pack** — the mechanics companion to `spec-driven-product`. Where the class playbook carries the judgment layer (doc-first, owner-owned expecteds), this pack carries the concrete framework standard so a new project or stack adopts it by convention: the `dev/requirements/` layout and shared leaf regex, `<slug>.<leaf-id>.case` naming with folder-as-kind classification, the coverage gate's full duty checklist (including manifest⇄disk equality for languages without dynamic import), the kind vocabulary, determinism rules (pinned clock, faked nondeterminism, real fonts, pixel-exact always), per-stack rendering recipes (jsdom+satori for DOM products, widget-test goldens for Flutter), the machine-managed gallery contract, and refresh-as-review-step.

It also standardizes the new **`saga` kind**: multi-step user stories rendered as ordered golden storyboards (`*.step-NN.png`) with narrative captions that surface in the spec's gallery — for requirements about *transitions and causality* ("a message sent before I arrived never appears") rather than resting states. First implementation: ShoutsAndWhispers `dev/requirements/saga/`.

**`flutter` pack: stub → earned rules** — ports-and-adapters out of the widget tree, widget-test/golden mechanics (FontManifest loading, no `pumpAndSettle` on spinners, injectable fetchers, fixed viewport, async-epoch guard), toolchain habits.

**`firebase` + `firebase-release` packs, and `android`/`ios`/`play-store-release`/`app-store-release` stubs** — Firebase rules/functions/deploy discipline; the opt-in dev/prod split standard (committed-default-dev, pipeline-injected prod config, App Check store attestation); registered stubs filled when first exercised.

**Corpus index** (`CLAUDE.md`) updated to route to the new packs.

## Verification

- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs skills/*/*.test.mjs` — 81/81 pass with the new packs present.
- `node checks/run.mjs` conformance sweep — clean (0 blocking, 0 advisory).
- Registry smoke: `loadPacks()` discovers `executable-requirements` + `firebase`; `detect` fires on the fingerprint files and not otherwise.
- Rebased onto latest `main` (linear, squash-friendly history).

Closes #180

{"number":567,"title":"Personal preferences as a pack, and one general primitive: a pack's own session-start step","body":"Personal interaction preferences are the concern of **one fleet's people**. The canon is mounted by every fleet that adopts Claudinite, which makes it both the wrong host for one group's preferences and the wrong authority on where they live — yet `preferences/<email>.md` sat here, and the session-start step fell back to a hardcoded `raw.githubusercontent.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/main/preferences` URL.

So the whole mechanism becomes **a pack**, and neither the engine nor the fleet enforcer learns what it is.

## The one thing core learns

The other end of the session already had the primitive: the SessionEnd runner discovers `session-end.mjs` in every active pack's directory, runs it bounded and fail-soft, and — in its own words — *"never names the pack whose step it runs, and never learns what one does."*

**`engine/pack_loader/run-pack-session-start.mjs`** is the symmetric half, on the same terms, with one difference: a session-start step's output *is* the contribution, so it is forwarded into the session context under the same `<!-- pack:id -->` marker the prose injector uses. It closes a real gap — prose is a **file**, fixed at vendor time and identical for every repo and person that mounts it, so a pack whose content is only knowable at session time had nowhere to put it but a core step naming that pack.

Two bounds keep the loan honest: every step is killed at a timeout, and its contribution is capped with the truncation stated in the injected text. Neither is a knob a pack can raise.

## The pack

`packs/claude-code-web-users-support/` — named for the **surface**, not the feature. A Claude Code *web* session runs for a signed-in person, in a managed container; a terminal session does neither. That difference is what makes a class of capability possible at all, and preferences are its first member.

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `pack.mjs` | `seededByDefault`, plus the adoption question that asks where the store is |
| `store.mjs` | the one resolver of the entry config, shared by the step and the rule |
| `session-start.mjs` | reads this user's file — local-first, then fetch, fail-soft at every miss |
| `store-configured.mjs` | one **advisory** rule, so a declared-but-unconfigured pack is not silently inert |
| `RULES.md` | the prose a session gets when the pack is active |

```json
{ "id": "claude-code-web-users-support", "config": { "repo": "missingbulb/Sheepdog" } }
```

**The engine now says nothing about preferences anywhere.** The setting, its resolver, its validation and the hook step are gone from `repo-context.mjs`, `engine/checks/README.md`, `bootstrap.md` and `vendoring/DESIGN.md`, replaced by the general contract. What the barriers rule already forbade — core naming a specific pack — is now true of this too.

## The enforcer doesn't know either

The sheepdog sweep first named the pack and carried its parameter, which made the enforcer a *second* place packs are known — the same coupling, one level out. So it is generalized:

| was | is |
|---|---|
| `fleet-preferences` | **`fleet-pack-seeds`** |
| `preferencesRepo: "…"` | **`packSeeds: [{ id, config? }]`** |

The sweep converges whatever declarations the **fleet** names in its own sheepdog config, and names no pack itself. Its contract is the migration op's, for the same reason: **seed, never override** — a member that already declares the pack, or already carries a config for it, keeps both. A test pins the constraint rather than trusting the prose: the sheepdog pack's sources may not contain the pack's name or the word "preferences" at all.

## The rollout: `declarePacks`, and a re-converge

The migration op follows the same move: **`settings`** (write a top-level key) becomes **`declarePacks`** (declare a pack and its config, seed-never-override). The record seeds the existing fleet with the store named.

That surfaced a real ordering bug in the class: **a declared pack whose code is not in the mount is a blocking `config` error**, and baselining vendors *before* it applies notes — so a seeded pack would red every member for a night. Baselining now **re-converges the mount when a note changed the declaration**, so both halves land in the one transactional commit. The rehearsal harness mirrors the same second pass (verified: the `re-converge` step fires and the fixture comes out green).

## What the owner has to do

**Nothing for today's fleet** — every member declares the pack on its next baselining, with the store named, mount and declaration in the same commit.

For the sweep to keep seeding afterwards (new members, a deleted entry), `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` needs Contents *write* across the owner's repos. Until then the sweep fails loudly and the scheduler converges a `needs-human` issue.

## Verification

- **1296 tests, 0 failures.** World sweep **0 blocking**.
- The runner's 8 tests were written first and watched fail; they cover discovery, activation gating, config hand-off, ordering, and every fail-soft path (crash, non-zero exit, hang, over-cap, silence).
- **Consumer rehearsal green** in all four fixture shapes × both modes — including the new re-converge.
- Live: the orchestrator runs `selftest, load-active-prose, pack-session-start, mount-skills, env-check, interview-check`, and the pack's step injects under `<!-- pack:claude-code-web-users-support -->`.
- Rebased onto `18b86a3`; the `agent_preprocessing` → `prework` rename main landed (#685) is adopted in the new task.

{"number":755,"title":"Promote two store/seed checks from Sheepdog PR #110 to the canon","body":"Sheepdog [#110](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/pull/110) proposed a local `preferences-store` pack and was closed. Its [closing comment](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/pull/110#issuecomment-5255280747) records that two of its checks are worth keeping but belong in the canon rather than in a member. This lands both, from that PR's diff.

## (a) `preferences-store-file-names` → `packs/claude-code-web-users-support/`

Every file in a preferences store is `README.md` or `<identity>.md`. That is a property of **being a store**, not of Sheepdog — the same feature the canon pack already owns.

- It sits beside `store.mjs` and imports `resolveStore` / `isUsableIdentity` as **siblings**, so it can never be stricter or looser than the code that opens a person's file. #110 had to reach across the vendored mount to get the same guarantee, which is exactly what forced it to carry a `file-placement` acceptance in `.claudinite-checks.json`; here there is nothing to excuse.
- **Advisory**, matching its sibling `store-configured` for the same reason: the loss is a nicety no other check or task depends on, and the fix is a rename.
- **Relevance-gated** on the repo actually holding the store directory its own declaration names, so it is inert in every member that merely declares the pack to *read* a store living elsewhere.
- It reads the store off `ctx.config.packConfig` — the engine's normalized per-pack view, the way `store-configured` does — rather than re-parsing `.claudinite-checks.json` as the local-pack version did.

## (b) `fleet-pack-seed-agrees` → `packs/sheepdog/`

The pack-agnostic form of #110's `store-address-agrees`. That version compared a `packSeeds` entry against the repo's own declaration of the pack, but hardcoded `claude-code-web-users-support` and `resolveStore`. Generalized: **for any seeded pack the enforcer also declares itself, the seed's config and the local config must agree.**

- Naming no pack preserves the sheepdog pack's deliberate design — the same "the enforcer names no pack" rule `fleet-config.mjs` and the seed sweep already hold to. The seeded ids are the whole vocabulary.
- Because it may not know any pack's defaults, agreement is **exact value equality** (key-order-insensitive). The cost is spelling a default out on both sides; the benefit is a comparison that cannot be wrong about a pack it has never heard of.
- **Blocking.** The seed sweep writes into every member and never overrides, so a wrong seed reaches the fleet once and then sticks — correcting it in the enforcer un-writes nothing.
- Seeds are read through `fleet-config.mjs`'s one parser, so the seeds judged are exactly the seeds that would be written (it drops the malformed ones); the local side is read through the engine's normalized config, the way a session in this repo actually runs the pack. A pack the fleet standardizes on but the enforcer does not itself declare is out of scope.

## consumer-safe-change: fixture, not a migration record

`fleet-pack-seed-agrees` is a new blocking rule, so `consumer-safe-change` asks for one of the two. **The fixture is the honest answer here** — the change is additive: nothing is renamed, and nothing new is required of a member that was already conforming. There is no fleet to move across, only a shape to prove stays green.

The new `sheepdog-enforcer` rehearsal shape is a repo declaring `sheepdog` with a `packSeeds` entry *and* its own declaration of the seeded pack — the two configs the rule now compares. They agree, so the enforcer converges green in both rehearsal modes. Confirmed the fixture actually exercises the rule rather than passing vacuously: making the two disagree turns the rehearsal red naming `fleet-pack-seed-agrees`, and it was then restored.

Checked the real fleet too — the one enforcer that exists today already states `{ "repo": "missingbulb/Sheepdog" }` on both sides, so nothing goes red overnight.

## Tests

Both see-it-fail fixtures come across, into `packs-tests/`, each asserting the claimed defect against the real reader (`store.mjs`'s `fileFor`; `parseSheepdogConfig`) rather than restating it. The seed fixture uses a made-up pack id throughout — a test reaching for a real one would quietly become a test of that pack.

Verified: full suite green (1415 tests before the rehearsal shape, 16/16 on the rehearsal gate after); `check_the_world.mjs` at 0 blocking with no new advisories; `check_the_work.mjs` clean. Each check was mutated to confirm its fixtures bite (accepting any `.md` name → 5 failures; comparing config presence instead of value → failures) before being restored.

Catalog tally moves 80 → 82, with the two per-pack counts in `packs/README.md`.

Prose: each check's `doc` pointer got the invariant it points at — the store-side naming rule in the web-users pack, the two-places-must-agree rule in sheepdog's — stated without narrating the enforcement (`pack-no-enforcement-narration` caught a first draft that named the rule id). # leaflet pack

Active when the repo references [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/): a CDN asset (`leaflet@` / `leaflet.js` / `leaflet.css`) in HTML, or an `L.map` / `L.tileLayer` / `L.markerClusterGroup` call in JS/TS source.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feature-detect a plugin, fall back to core | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| An embedded map sets scrollWheelZoom false | medium | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Keep the tile provider's attribution | critical | legal | prose: <100 words + check (`leaflet/tile-attribution`) |
| Transform a marker's inner element | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `leaflet/asset-integrity` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `leaflet/tile-attribution` | critical | legal | check: blocking |
==========
# google-identity pack

Declared for a backend that **validates Google Sign-In (Google Identity) ID tokens** — an API
Gateway JWT authorizer, or any OIDC verifier whose issuer is the Google accounts origin. No
reliable structural fingerprint, so it is declared by hand. **Prose-free:** the pack mounts the
[`google-id-token-validation`](skills/google-id-token-validation/SKILL.md) skill, whose
check-the-work rules run at every Stop and in CI — each failure message is the rule.

Scope: the **validator** side of Google auth — not obtaining the ID token in a browser or
extension client.

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `google-token-audience-pinned` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `google-token-email-verified` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `google-client-id-single-origin` | medium | correctness | check: advisory |
==========
# executable-requirements pack

Active when the repo has `dev/requirements/requirements.md`. The concrete framework standard for
running a spec as tests: layout, case naming, the coverage gate's duties, the kind vocabulary
(including the storyboard `saga` kind), the machine-managed gallery, and the determinism rules that
make rendered expecteds byte-stable. Prose-only: every rule here is enforced by gates **the
declaring project itself commits** (coverage gate, gallery gate) — the pack standardizes what those
gates must check, not the checking.

The judgment layer above it — doc-first discipline, owner-owned expecteds, honest-gap tracking —
is not here.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

The always-on rules — the layout every case lands in, the gallery and the refresh lane:

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|

leaf-line convention and the kind vocabulary in `write-a-requirement-leaf`, the storyboard and
animated-golden rules in `write-a-saga`, the determinism rules and the per-stack rendering recipes
in `deterministic-expecteds`.

- **Requirement lines** are parsed with one shared regex (`` ^\s*(?:-\s+)?`(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)` ``)

{"number":956,"title":"Converge the clone's git config at session start, not in the pasted setup script","body":"Fixes #955.

**Is the script still needed?** Yes — it is the only thing that installs an active pack's declared toolchain (the Flutter SDK, node deps) into the web environment *image*, which a per-session hook cannot do. What it does *not* need to carry is per-clone git config or a description of the mount it runs on.

### The git config moves to a managed place
`git config merge.ours.driver true` / `rerere.enabled true` configured the checkout, but ran once at environment-image build time and only in a repo whose owner had pasted the script — a terminal clone never got it, and a re-cloned checkout lost it. Both now run as a fail-soft `git-config` step in `engine/hooks/session-start-command.sh`, first in the converge group: vendored, so every member gets it on its next mount refresh, and no re-paste is needed. No repo at `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` logs a line and returns 0; the step writes nothing into the session context.

### The script shrinks 34 lines → 16
Removed: the legacy fetch-at-session-start caveat (retired with vendoring phase 3, 2026-07-21), the restatement of how `env-requirements.mjs` works (`bootstrap.md` Part 9 and `packs/README.md` own it), and the two git-config lines. Kept: what it is, that its body is pasted into the environment's Setup script field, and that it runs as root in the checkout's parent.

### Also corrected
- `bootstrap.md` Part 9 named the wrong vendored path (`engine/vendoring/` → `engine/hooks/`).
- The `generated-merge-driver` check's `fix` no longer tells the reader to run a one-time `git config` the hook now performs.

### Verification
- New test in `engine-tests/hooks/session-start-command.test.mjs` asserts the config is actually set in a real `git init` repo and that the no-repo path is silent; watched both assertions fail with the step stashed out.
- Full suite `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`: 2006 pass, 0 fail.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking; the 61 advisories are pre-existing and none anchor to the touched files.

Every touched pack README's rule table was reconciled 1:1 against its `RULES.md`; the skills index and pack directory were regenerated.

{"number":128,"title":"Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement","body":"## What this is

Reorganizes the corpus from always/soft-loaded instructions into **two homes selected by *when* a rule is active**, plus a deterministic enforcement engine:

- **`packs/<name>/`** — a bundle of prose (`RULES.md`) *and* checks, active **once per session** by the project's `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration (`universal` always on). Active packs' prose is injected by a SessionStart hook; their checks run at every Stop and in CI. A dependency-free registry discovers packs by directory scan — no list to maintain.
- **`skills/<name>/`** — activity-scoped procedures the harness surfaces on demand; content inlined in each `SKILL.md` (no cross-tree redirect).
- **`checks/`** — the engine only: the runner, lib, the Stop hook, the PreToolUse guard, and their red-first fixtures.

`always/`, `tasks/`, `technologies/`, and `templates/` are gone — folded into the two homes.

## The model (design in `checks/DESIGN.md`)

- **Promotion ladder**: platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose. A rule lives in the cheapest mechanism that can carry it; prose is the audited fallback.
- **Checks** are declared+closed (every rule of a declared pack runs every time), drift-guarded by a structural fingerprint meta-check; diff-scoped only as a transitional aid (whole-repo sweep is the default); reasoned acceptances; fail-fast severity (advisory is a per-rule *kind*, not a burn-in stage).
- **Platform settings are verified, never trusted** — an offline effect check (squash-only ⇒ no merge commits in main's first-parent history) plus a config check later.
- **Technology gotchas convert per-gotcha** by whether they have a static artifact signature; the rest is pack prose.
- **Skills**: model-invoked routing is probabilistic, so nothing that *must* happen rides on a skill — enforcement is checks/hooks/settings. (Skill-scoped hooks exist, verified, for the rare activity-scoped enforcement need.)
- **Growth is checks-first**: promote descends the ladder for each new lesson; a `prose-to-checks` skill sweeps the existing prose backlog for always-testable rules the conversion missed.

## Implemented (all green: 42 tests, CI passing, sweep clean)

- Runner + registry; **universal pack** (7 checks) + **github-actions** (6) + **chrome-extension** conformance (6); the pack-prose SessionStart loader; the Stop hook and PreToolUse guard.
- Full pack prose (baseline, technology packs, the chrome-extension release standard, the research-project class pack); 12 inlined skills (command + practice) + the prose-to-checks skill.
- Bootstrap Parts 6–7 (hooks, `--init`, skill symlinks); index, README, DESIGN, growth docs all updated to the two-home model.

## The checks earned their keep repeatedly

They caught real defects at every stage — dangling links and a label/href mismatch on `main`; **nine historical merge commits** that had bypassed the squash-only policy unnoticed (now sha-keyed acceptances); real pipefail defects in the canon release workflows; and several of my own regressions mid-restructure (the Stop hook blocked me in-session more than once).

**Owner action outstanding:** flip the squash-only merge *setting* (repo Settings → General) — unreachable from here; the effect check covers the gap meanwhile.

Closes #127
Closes #131

## What each pack's history turned out to be

**executable-requirements** (14 files). One origin plus five decisions. #165 opened the pack whole, and its body splits the attribution by facet — GoogleCalendarEventCreator (origin, jsdom rendering), TLDR (the cross-tier `server` kind), ShoutsAndWhispers (Flutter port, first `saga`). I put the wholesale attribution on the commit's defaults fence and overrode it only where the evidence names a project for that element: ShoutsAndWhispers on `write-a-saga` and `flutter-rule`, GoogleCalendarEventCreator on `browser-extension-dom` (whose "no real browser: deterministic and dependency-light at a documented fidelity tradeoff" is a real `Rejected`). #206 added the animated APNG saga golden, with GIF rejected for non-deterministic palette/dithering. #311 bore `feature-requirements-first` on the then-new conversation surface; #338 widened its gate after CrosswordChat hit a finding no commit could clear, rejecting the `accept` and the post-hoc rebase. #401 added the adoption interview and the one-liner/kind-selection conventions. #1060 (neighbour prose), #1634 (`RULES.md` framing) and #1667 (three path-forced skills) follow. The ten elements the brief drafted as born in #1667 are written `born` in #165 where the lesson entered the pack and `moved` in #1667; the shared bar for that move ("a rule leaves RULES.md only where forced paths cover every moment it is needed") is written once on `deterministic-expecteds` and cited from the other nine.

**leaflet** (7 files + a new `_declined.md`). All five rules born together in #403, a weekly pack-discovery run against EdFringeNow, each grounded in a named file of that site. #467 cut the grounded-in notes and the consequence prose; #1575 recovered the rationale for two rules and re-confirmed the notes stay cut (#1571) — both on `_pack`. The CDN pin+SRI rule converted at #510; the tile-attribution rule converted at #607 after #510 had weighed it and left it as prose (the out-of-band `addAttribution` guard is what made the detection confident) — both carry the deletion-test verdict and what grepping would have answered instead. #510's three deliberately-unconverted rules are the `_declined.md` entry.

**google-identity** (4 files). Effectively one pull request: #350 bore the pack from TLDR's API Gateway JWT authorizer to home the validator side (the client side was already homed), opened it as three prose rules and converted them to skill-owned checks in the same PR when the owner's direction reversed the "no reliable signature" judgment. The skill's entry records why it names none of its own rule ids (enforcement silence). #839 moved both checks' gates onto shared file classes and structural self-exclusion; #1060 removed the neighbour pack from README and SKILL.md.

## Where the brief's derivation was wrong, and the proof

1. **`Closes` vs `Refs`** — the brief reads the commit trailer; the PR bodies disagree four times: #165 `Closes #180`, #311 `Fixes #310` + `Closes #314`, #1667 `Closes #1662` (GitHub's `closed_by_pull_requests` on issue #1662 agrees), #1634 `Closes #1632`. Read every body with `pull_request_read`.
2. **"version rows no commit here claims"** — `60902.1` was listed unclaimed for *both* executable-requirements and leaflet. `git show aaa7938b -- packs/<pack>/VERSIONS.md` shows #1634 adding the row in both.
3. **`marker-needs-css` drafted `born` at #467** — `git show b5103ea4:packs/leaflet/RULES.md` has it in full at #403; #467 only shortened its trigger sentence, which is what the brief matches elements by. Written as born in #403.
4. **Both google-identity checks drafted `born` at #827** — they are coded rules in #350's `checks.mjs`; #790 re-expressed them as declarations and #827 moved those to JSON, neither changing what they demand ("nothing behavioural moves"). Written as born in #350, and I wrote no entry for #790/#827 since re-expressing a rule as data decides nothing about it.
5. **`feature-requirements-first` at #338 drafted `reworded`** — it changed the check's gate, so `severity-changed`.
6. **The ten #1667 elements drafted `born`** — `moved`, with `born` back-dated to #165.

## Decisions I could not attribute

- `artifact-expecteds-live`, `feature-detect-optional`, `marker-needs-css`, `pin-clock`, `fake-nondeterministic-input`, `wait-settled`, `whatever-stack` and `deterministic-expecteds` have no recorded rationale anywhere — not in the PR bodies, not in a deleted `references.md` (executable-requirements and google-identity never had one; `git log --diff-filter=D` confirms only leaflet's). They get short `born` entries with date, actor, model, mechanism and landed, and no invented `Reason`.
- `folder-kind` and `load-real-fonts` DO have recoverable reasons — the clauses #467 cut ("so classification cannot drift", "making goldens unreviewable"). Recovered from the pre-#467 text and marked as such, as the earlier html backfill did.
- I recorded no per-element entry for #467's corpus-wide tightening or #350's enforcement-narration trim of exec-req's `RULES.md`: neither changed what the carrier decides. #467's leaflet-specific decision (the grounded-in notes) is on `_pack`, since the commit names leaflet for it.

## Verification

`provenance.mjs check` on each pack: full listing, no fault, exit 0. Offline suite (322 files): 3808 pass / 0 fail. `check_the_world`: exit 0, 0 blocking, 47 advisory, none naming my three packs — all three have left the `provenance-integrity` list. `check_the_work`: exit 0, 2 advisory, both `provenance-change-recorded` on the two leaflet files the references conversion had filled — the rewrite the skill sanctions and the check's own fix text names; said so in the PR body. `git status --porcelain` shows only `provenance/`, `README.md`, `pack.mjs` under the three packs. No version bumped, no `VERSIONS.md` touched, no carrier changed, no long dash in any added line.

Byte table (before → after): exec-req README 4267→3605, pack.mjs 2463→1830; leaflet README 1332→897, pack.mjs 1554→1025; google-identity README 1050→901, pack.mjs 1332→771.

## On the coordinator's mid-run note

All four points were already handled: the Closes/Refs sweep, the mis-dated births (proved with `git show <sha>:<old path>`), the claimed version rows, and the truncate-then-apply remedy for the two conversion-filled leaflet files (read first, `Reason` and `Retire when` relocated onto the `born` entries they evidence, nothing dropped). On the fourth point I re-checked all three READMEs after trimming: their tables are rule/check/skill catalogs with no history, and no cross-reference dangles — the two "above"/"below" phrases left in exec-req's README still resolve.

## Things worth fixing upstream

- **The brief's element-birth derivation is systematically early-biased**: it names an element by the file carrying it today, so every rule that later moved into a skill, or converted from a coded module to a declaration, drafts `born` at the move. That is three of my three packs. The skill's step 3 hints at it ("a row reading NOTHING DRAFTED… read its files"), but the misleading rows here were the *drafted* ones, not the NOTHING-DRAFTED ones. Worth stating in step 4 outright: verify every `born` against `git show <sha>^:<old path>` before accepting it.
- **The skill's step 5 sentence about shared `Source`** ("where the pack's evidence names a member per rule rather than rule by rule") reads backwards on first pass — the two halves of the contrast are easy to swap. It cost me a re-read.
- **`provenance.mjs check` does not name a skill's coded check module.** `google-client-id-single-origin`, the advisory check in `packs/google-identity/skills/google-id-token-validation/checks.mjs`, has no provenance file, and `check` reports no fault for it — so the backfill had nothing to append to and the pack's README lists a check whose history is unrecorded. Flagged in the PR body; it is a marking-pass gap, not this run's to fix.

Verified all three against the PR bodies: #165 `Closes #180`, #1667 `Closes #1662`, #128 `Closes #127` + `Closes #131`. My merged [#2213](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2213) writes `Refs` for all of them — eleven `Landed` lines across four files. I found that exact bug on host-page, credited the Opus run for catching it, and then took the brief's default anyway on the next run. It's a fidelity loss, not a structural one: `Closes` is what actually linked PR to issue, so a reader tracing which issue a pack closed gets the wrong answer.

I'm not fixing it yet — the three agents still running may carry the same slip, and one sweep over all of it beats five. It needs its own PR and its own approval regardless.

**Two PRs open so far:**

- **[#2215](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2215)** — `node`, `numpy-image-processing`. Found nine `Closes`/`Refs` errors, a `born` sitting on the wrong commit (`node-test-skips` was born at #751, not #1667 — the brief names an element by the file carrying it *today*), and one claimed version row. `numpy`'s evidence turned out to be per-rule, citing the exact member file and function behind each, so it correctly refused one shared `Source`.
- **[#2216](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2216)** — `jwt`, `python`, `ios`. Found eight more misplaced `born` entries (jwt's five checks were coded modules at #705 before #839 converted them to declarations), five claimed version rows, and a genuine `Rejected` on jwt's `_pack`. It also caught a slip in its own shipped work — one of ten PR bodies it took from the trailer — and flagged it rather than letting it ride. It's pushing that one-line fix now.

Three structural findings worth filing once the fan-out is done:

1. **`python`'s two checks have no provenance file at all**, and `check` neither lists nor faults them. The carrier scan reads check ids with a literal regex over a skill's `checks.mjs`; python's is a two-line aggregator that re-exports from two modules, so the ids are invisible and the marking pass skipped them. Their decisions have nowhere to land.
2. **A `retired` element can never receive its history** — `apply`/`append` refuse a file that doesn't exist, and the marking pass only created files for live carriers, yet the convention says a retired element's file stays. That's how jwt's deleted `jwt-advisory-watch` task ended up homeless.
3. **`apply` refuses an entry dated before the file's last one**, so a `references.md`-converted file can't receive an honest earlier `born` by the obvious route. The remedy is to truncate first — which the convention sanctions but the skill never says.

> ⚠️ Still open: three agents running (website family, exec-req/leaflet/google-identity, claudinite-* packs). [#2215](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2215) and [#2216](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2216) open, unreviewed, nothing merged. My `Closes`/`Refs` error stands in merged `main` until the sweep — eleven lines in four files under `packs/android`, `packs/app-store-release`, `packs/play-store-release`, `packs/html`. One origin plus five decisions. #165 opened the pack whole, and its body splits the attribution by facet — GoogleCalendarEventCreator (origin, jsdom rendering), TLDR (the cross-tier `server` kind), ShoutsAndWhispers (Flutter port, first `saga`). I put the wholesale attribution on the commit's defaults fence and overrode it only where the evidence names a project for that element: ShoutsAndWhispers on `write-a-saga` and `flutter-rule`, GoogleCalendarEventCreator on `browser-extension-dom` (whose "no real browser: deterministic and dependency-light at a documented fidelity tradeoff" is a real `Rejected`). #206 added the animated APNG saga golden, with GIF rejected for non-deterministic palette/dithering. #311 bore `feature-requirements-first` on the then-new conversation surface; #338 widened its gate after CrosswordChat hit a finding no commit could clear, rejecting the `accept` and the post-hoc rebase. #401 added the adoption interview and the one-liner/kind-selection conventions. #1060 (neighbour prose), #1634 (`RULES.md` framing) and #1667 (three path-forced skills) follow. The ten elements the brief drafted as born in #1667 are written `born` in #165 where the lesson entered the pack and `moved` in #1667; the shared bar for that move ("a rule leaves RULES.md only where forced paths cover every moment it is needed") is written once on `deterministic-expecteds` and cited from the other nine.
  
  **leaflet** (7 files + a new `_declined.md`). All five rules born together in #403, a weekly pack-discovery run against EdFringeNow, each grounded in a named file of that site. #467 cut the grounded-in notes and the consequence prose; #1575 recovered the rationale for two rules and re-confirmed the notes stay cut (#1571) — both on `_pack`. The CDN pin+SRI rule converted at #510; the tile-attribution rule converted at #607 after #510 had weighed it and left it as prose (the out-of-band `addAttribution` guard is what made the detection confident) — both carry the deletion-test verdict and what grepping would have answered instead. #510's three deliberately-unconverted rules are the `_declined.md` entry.
  
  **google-identity** (4 files). Effectively one pull request: #350 bore the pack from TLDR's API Gateway JWT authorizer to home the validator side (the client side was already homed), opened it as three prose rules and converted them to skill-owned checks in the same PR when the owner's direction reversed the "no reliable signature" judgment. The skill's entry records why it names none of its own rule ids (enforcement silence). #839 moved both checks' gates onto shared file classes and structural self-exclusion; #1060 removed the neighbour pack from README and SKILL.md.
  
  ## Where the brief's derivation was wrong, and the proof
  
  1. **`Closes` vs `Refs`** — the brief reads the commit trailer; the PR bodies disagree four times: #165 `Closes #180`, #311 `Fixes #310` + `Closes #314`, #1667 `Closes #1662` (GitHub's `closed_by_pull_requests` on issue #1662 agrees), #1634 `Closes #1632`. Read every body with `pull_request_read`.
  2. **"version rows no commit here claims"** — `60902.1` was listed unclaimed for *both* executable-requirements and leaflet. `git show aaa7938b -- packs/<pack>/VERSIONS.md` shows #1634 adding the row in both.
  3. **`marker-needs-css` drafted `born` at #467** — `git show b5103ea4:packs/leaflet/RULES.md` has it in full at #403; #467 only shortened its trigger sentence, which is what the brief matches elements by. Written as born in #403.
  4. **Both google-identity checks drafted `born` at #827** — they are coded rules in #350's `checks.mjs`; #790 re-expressed them as declarations and #827 moved those to JSON, neither changing what they demand ("nothing behavioural moves"). Written as born in #350, and I wrote no entry for #790/#827 since re-expressing a rule as data decides nothing about it.
  5. **`feature-requirements-first` at #338 drafted `reworded`** — it changed the check's gate, so `severity-changed`.
  6. **The ten #1667 elements drafted `born`** — `moved`, with `born` back-dated to #165.
  
  ## Decisions I could not attribute
  
  - `artifact-expecteds-live`, `feature-detect-optional`, `marker-needs-css`, `pin-clock`, `fake-nondeterministic-input`, `wait-settled`, `whatever-stack` and `deterministic-expecteds` have no recorded rationale anywhere — not in the PR bodies, not in a deleted `references.md` (executable-requirements and google-identity never had one; `git log --diff-filter=D` confirms only leaflet's). They get short `born` entries with date, actor, model, mechanism and landed, and no invented `Reason`.
  - `folder-kind` and `load-real-fonts` DO have recoverable reasons — the clauses #467 cut ("so classification cannot drift", "making goldens unreviewable"). Recovered from the pre-#467 text and marked as such, as the earlier html backfill did.
  - I recorded no per-element entry for #467's corpus-wide tightening or #350's enforcement-narration trim of exec-req's `RULES.md`: neither changed what the carrier decides. #467's leaflet-specific decision (the grounded-in notes) is on `_pack`, since the commit names leaflet for it.
  
  ## Verification
  
  `provenance.mjs check` on each pack: full listing, no fault, exit 0. Offline suite (322 files): 3808 pass / 0 fail. `check_the_world`: exit 0, 0 blocking, 47 advisory, none naming my three packs — all three have left the `provenance-integrity` list. `check_the_work`: exit 0, 2 advisory, both `provenance-change-recorded` on the two leaflet files the references conversion had filled — the rewrite the skill sanctions and the check's own fix text names; said so in the PR body. `git status --porcelain` shows only `provenance/`, `README.md`, `pack.mjs` under the three packs. No version bumped, no `VERSIONS.md` touched, no carrier changed, no long dash in any added line.
  
  Byte table (before → after): exec-req README 4267→3605, pack.mjs 2463→1830; leaflet README 1332→897, pack.mjs 1554→1025; google-identity README 1050→901, pack.mjs 1332→771.
  
  ## On the coordinator's mid-run note
  
  All four points were already handled: the Closes/Refs sweep, the mis-dated births (proved with `git show <sha>:<old path>`), the claimed version rows, and the truncate-then-apply remedy for the two conversion-filled leaflet files (read first, `Reason` and `Retire when` relocated onto the `born` entries they evidence, nothing dropped). On the fourth point I re-checked all three READMEs after trimming: their tables are rule/check/skill catalogs with no history, and no cross-reference dangles — the two "above"/"below" phrases left in exec-req's README still resolve.
  
  ## Things worth fixing upstream
  
  - **The brief's element-birth derivation is systematically early-biased**: it names an element by the file carrying it today, so every rule that later moved into a skill, or converted from a coded module to a declaration, drafts `born` at the move. That is three of my three packs. The skill's step 3 hints at it ("a row reading NOTHING DRAFTED… read its files"), but the misleading rows here were the *drafted* ones, not the NOTHING-DRAFTED ones. Worth stating in step 4 outright: verify every `born` against `git show <sha>^:<old path>` before accepting it.
  - **The skill's step 5 sentence about shared `Source`** ("where the pack's evidence names a member per rule rather than rule by rule") reads backwards on first pass — the two halves of the contrast are easy to swap. It cost me a re-read.
  - **`provenance.mjs check` does not name a skill's coded check module.** `google-client-id-single-origin`, the advisory check in `packs/google-identity/skills/google-id-token-validation/checks.mjs`, has no provenance file, and `check` reports no fault for it — so the backfill had nothing to append to and the pack's README lists a check whose history is unrecorded. Flagged in the PR body; it is a marking-pass gap, not this run's to fix.

Advances #2169. It closes nothing: #2169 tracks the backfill across the whole shelf, and this is three packs of it.

## What the history carries

**`jwt`** (15 files). One birth and two later decisions. The pack was born whole in #705 from *The JWT Handbook*, with token budget as the design constraint: no session-start prose at all, five checks whose failure message is the rule, and two skills read only at usage time for the judgment half. The PR body's per-rule table gives each check its own book section, so those went on the checks rather than on the shared fence. #839 converted all five from coded rule modules into `declared-checks.json` declarations, deleting both `checks.mjs` files and the pack-local `scan.mjs`. #1569 retired `jwt-advisory-watch` and moved the duty to canon curation's upstream task, which is the `## Upstream` section's whole reason for existing; that went on `_pack.md` as a `moved`.

**`python`** (5 files). Born in #345 from `missingbulb/LaughCounter` by a `growth-discover` run, with one routing decision running through the whole pack: the repo's own `pyproject.toml` names exactly which packages are optional, so the two mechanical rules had a false-positive-free signal and became checks, while "which deps count as heavy", the stdlib-backend architecture and the F401 probe had none and stayed prose. Each rule then took three or four more decisions: #467 cut its consequence prose, #1634 turned the three section-shaped rules into trigger-keyed bullets at the ration, #1647 cut the skill's self-describing opening, and #1667 moved `adding-heavy-native` into the skill under the owner's path-forced bar while explicitly leaving `importing-module-only` in prose (recorded as `reaffirmed`, with the reason the audit gave).

**`ios`** (3 files). Read consistently with `android`'s file from #2213, and verified against `ios`'s own diffs at each step: born as a registered stub in #165 with ShoutsAndWhispers' iOS configuration at its Firebase release milestone as the expected first material, `reworded` by #1634's framing drop, `moved` by #1667 when the stub note went to the README and `RULES.md` was deleted. `ios` then diverges from `android`: #1671 filled the stub with its first two rules, so `_pack.md` takes a fourth entry for the stub framing leaving the manifest. The rules' text was written by the `growth-promote` run of 2026-08-22 on the branch of #1204, which was closed in favour of #1671; `Landed` names #1671, where the text reached `main`, and `Source` names the run and its members as a set, which is as fine as the evidence goes.

## Corrections to the brief's derivation

- **`Closes` vs `Refs`.** The brief derives `Landed` from the commit trailer, which said `Refs` for five pull requests whose bodies say `Closes`: #705 (`Closes #706`), #467 (`Closes #466`), #1634 (`Closes #1632`), #1667 (`Closes #1662`), #165 (`Closes #180`). The bodies are authoritative, so the entries carry `Closes`. Note that `packs/android/provenance/_pack.md` and its siblings from #2213 carry `Refs #180`, `Refs #1632` and `Refs #1662` for the same three pull requests; that is worth a later correcting entry on those files, not a rewrite here.
- **Ten cited pull requests, nine bodies read.** Of the ten pull requests these entries cite, nine had their bodies read directly. #1647's was taken from its commit trailer, which says `Refs #1646` where the body says `Closes #1646` - the same trap as the bullet above, caught after the first push and corrected in a follow-up commit on this branch. The near-miss is the point: the trailer and the body disagree often enough that reading the trailer is not a shortcut, it is a wrong answer roughly half the time on the older pull requests.
- **Five `born` entries dated to the wrong commit.** The brief drafted `jwt`'s five checks as `born` at #839, because it names a check by the `declared-checks.json` that carries it today. `git show 'a5aeab8e^:packs/jwt/skills/jwt-validation/none-not-accepted.mjs'` shows the same ids, severities and messages living as coded rule modules since #705, so each file takes a `born` at #705 and a `converted` at #839.
- **Three `born` entries dated to the wrong commit.** Same shape in `python`: the brief drafted `importing-module-only` and `wrapping-heavy-backend` as `born` at #1634 and `adding-heavy-native` as `born` at #1667. `git show c5b1eb3a:packs/python/RULES.md` shows all three as prose sections at #345; #1634 reworded them into bullets and #1667 moved one into the skill.
- **Four version rows listed as claimed by no commit are claimed.** `git log -S` on each row's own text names the commit that added it: jwt 60901.1 → #1569, jwt 60823.1 → #1262, python 60902.1 → #1634, python 60903.1 → #1647, ios 60902.1 → #1634.

## Bytes before and after

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/jwt/README.md` | 2174 | 1893 |
| `packs/jwt/pack.mjs` | 1904 | 1220 |
| `packs/python/README.md` | 2271 | 1219 |
| `packs/python/pack.mjs` | 1657 | 1053 |
| `packs/ios/README.md` | 628 | 598 |
| `packs/ios/pack.mjs` | 557 | 557 (already one line; nothing to move) |

What moved out: jwt's `_Provenance: distilled from…_` line and the manifest's paragraph on why JWT practice needs an upstream declaration; python's whole `**Provenance.**` paragraph, the "which is what makes … a false-positive-free signal" justification under Checks, and the manifest's account of what mechanized and what stayed prose; ios's "filled from worked examples as a project first exercises this for real". jwt's Upstream entry for the Handbook pointed at "this pack's provenance above", which the trim removed, so it now names the book on its own line.

## Verification

- `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs check jwt|python|ios` - the full file-to-carrier listing, no fault, exit 0 for each; every file now names a carrier and none is empty.

input.title: Provenance: backfill public-website, github-pages, cloudflare-site, cloudflare-workers
input.head: claude/backfill-website-packs
input.body:
Four packs in one pull request because three of them are one decision: #2101 split `static-website` by ownership into `public-website` (its rename), `github-pages` and `cloudflare-site`, and `cloudflare-workers` is the sibling `cloudflare-site` draws its fingerprint boundary against. Reading that pull request once served all four.

This advances #2169 and closes nothing.

## What the history turned out to be, per pack

### `public-website`

Not born at #2101. It is the rename of `static-website`, so `_pack` runs back through thirteen version rows to #611 (`Closes #609`): one pack for a whole static-site flow, its explicit publish set chosen over "the repo root minus what we remember to hide", fingerprinted by the vendored orchestrator. Then `requires` drops `github-actions` at #1081, the manifest stops restating its own tree at #1248, `RULES.md` drops its descriptive framing at #1634, and #2101 splits it.

The four client-side caching rules are older than the split too: born together at #727, from a named live outage in `missingbulb/EdFringeNow` (#309, fixed in #310) where 4,122 listings drew as sold out mid-season and 94% of a 60,115-row join came back status-unknown with no error, no console line and no network request. That incident is one shared `Source` on the commit's defaults fence rather than four paraphrases. #2101 reworded all four to the ration. `judging-failed-fetch` carries the `basics` placement that was weighed and turned down; the four-way "no new checks, these are judgements about a design" verdict is on `_declined.md`, with the one candidate #727 left open for revisiting.

`writing-version-number` and the `version-stamp-matches-package` check are not this pack's own births either: both arrived from `cloudflare-site` (#1982) in #2101, when versioning stopped being a hosting pack's business.

### `github-pages`

The pack is genuinely new at #2101, but two of its carriers are not. The subpath rule was born in `static-website` at #611 and moved here with the serving half. The skill descends from `RELEASE.md` (#611) through `static-site-releases` (#1056), a reword at #1647, its `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` trigger at #1650, and the managed-copies rule moving out of `RULES.md` into its body at #1667, before becoming `github-pages-pipeline` at #2101. The two checks and the `site-release` task are born at #2101, the task's shape taken from `cloudflare-site`'s and its declaration rationale read off its own task README. #2182's cadence change is a `policy-changed` on the task.

### `cloudflare-site`

Born at #1982 (`Closes #1981`), generalized out of ClaudiniteWebsite's local pack, asking its adopters nothing because the published tree, the hostnames and the analytics choice are all already structural in the repo. `no-second-publisher` carries the owner's own words for why the previous host's leftovers are detected rather than listed as adoption steps. #2100 is a real `_pack` decision the brief left undrafted: the version minor gained a year offset because a bare `MMDD` runs backwards every New Year. #2101 split the versioning half out into `public-website`'s seam, leaving a delegating shim whose retirement is #2113.

### `cloudflare-workers`

One commit, 91df7ff1, landed by the `growth-discover-packs` run in #1780 (`Refs #642`). Eleven rules, each traceable to a specific artifact in `missingbulb/hitbut` or `missingbulb/WIP`'s `backend/` — that per-member mapping came off the README's evidence table and is now the per-rule `Source`. The rules had no recorded rationale beyond their own text, so their entries are short by design rather than padded. #1982 added one `_pack` entry: the routing guidance's `excludes` repointed from `static-website` to the new `cloudflare-site` sibling.

## Corrections to the brief's derivation

- **`Landed` keywords.** The brief derived `Refs #1981` for #1982 from the commit trailer; the pull request body says `Closes #1981`, and the body wins. #611 likewise carries `Closes #609`, #2182 `Closes #1995`. #2101 and #727 carry no closing keyword at all, so neither entry claims one.
- **`cloudflare-workers` was credited to a bare commit.** The brief's `Landed` read `commit 91df7ff1 (Refs #642)`. 91df7ff1 landed through #1780, which is what the unclaimed version row `60906.1` names; the entries cite the pull request, and `Actor` is the run plus who merged it.
- **#2100 read as NOTHING DRAFTED.** It touched only `bump-version.mjs`, so no carrier's text moved, but its commit body records a genuine decision about the version scheme's shape. It is now an entry on `cloudflare-site`'s `_pack`.
- **A `git log --grep` finds the wrong commit for the rules cut.** The squash commit for #2101 carries every sub-commit's message, so subject matching is useless inside it; the sub-commits were fetched by head sha (`1a410b80`) and each entry's `Model` taken from the sub-commit that actually made the change (Opus 5 for the rules cut, Fable 5.1 for the rename and the versioning move) rather than from the squash trailer's flat list.
- **The `references.md` files were read out of git before anything was truncated**, so nothing the conversion carried was dropped rather than relocated. `github-pages`' and `cloudflare-site`' deleted `references.md` were also the proof that the skill, the task and three rules never had a recorded rationale, rather than an assumption that they did.

## README and `pack.mjs` bytes

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/public-website/README.md` | 2396 | 2274 |
| `packs/public-website/pack.mjs` | 1287 | 988 |
| `packs/github-pages/README.md` | 3493 | 3088 |
| `packs/github-pages/pack.mjs` | 3272 | 2704 |
| `packs/cloudflare-site/README.md` | 3353 | 3157 |
| `packs/cloudflare-site/pack.mjs` | 4073 | 3474 |
| `packs/cloudflare-workers/README.md` | 3260 | 1758 |
| `packs/cloudflare-workers/pack.mjs` | 1304 | 1059 |

What moved: each manifest's "WHAT IS NOT HERE" and fingerprint-justification paragraphs, `public-website`'s New Year rationale for the version scheme, `github-pages`' relevance-gate and skill-triggering reasons, `cloudflare-site`'s "a checklist of no-ops teaches its reader to skim it", and `cloudflare-workers`' whole per-member evidence table — a table is history too, even though the brief's README-sections list excludes tables. `cloudflare-workers`' and `cloudflare-site`' **Upstream** reconciliation anchors stayed: that section is live state the `revalidate-from-source` task maintains, not a decision.

## Verification

- `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs check <pack>` for all four: the full file-to-carrier listing with no `(empty)` and no fault, exit 0 each.
- Full offline suite, 322 test files: **3808 tests, 3808 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: exit 0, and no finding names any of the four packs.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs`: exit 0, 0 blocking, 13 advisory — one `provenance-change-recorded` per file the `references.md` conversion had filled and this backfill rewrote. That is the case the check's own fix text sanctions ("leave it where the rewrite is the correct history (the backfill replacing what the conversion wrote) and let the diff be the record"), so it is left standing.
- `git status --porcelain` shows only `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` under the four packs. No carrier text, no check, no skill trigger and no task policy is changed; no pack version is bumped and no `VERSIONS.md` is touched.

## Predicted automerge policy

`packs/public-website/`, `packs/github-pages/`, `packs/cloudflare-site/` and `packs/cloudflare-workers/`, each limited to `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs`.

toolu_01827VV7tsDCiL7cDu3kWdSs.body:
Four packs in one pull request because three of them are one decision: #2101 split `static-website` by ownership into `public-website` (its rename), `github-pages` and `cloudflare-site`, and `cloudflare-workers` is the sibling `cloudflare-site` draws its fingerprint boundary against. Reading that pull request once served all four.

This advances #2169 and closes nothing.

## What the history turned out to be, per pack

### `public-website`

Not born at #2101. It is the rename of `static-website`, so `_pack` runs back through thirteen version rows to #611 (`Closes #609`): one pack for a whole static-site flow, its explicit publish set chosen over "the repo root minus what we remember to hide", fingerprinted by the vendored orchestrator. Then `requires` drops `github-actions` at #1081, the manifest stops restating its own tree at #1248, `RULES.md` drops its descriptive framing at #1634, and #2101 splits it.

The four client-side caching rules are older than the split too: born together at #727, from a named live outage in `missingbulb/EdFringeNow` (#309, fixed in #310) where 4,122 listings drew as sold out mid-season and 94% of a 60,115-row join came back status-unknown with no error, no console line and no network request. That incident is one shared `Source` on the commit's defaults fence rather than four paraphrases. #2101 reworded all four to the ration. `judging-failed-fetch` carries the `basics` placement that was weighed and turned down; the four-way "no new checks, these are judgements about a design" verdict is on `_declined.md`, with the one candidate #727 left open for revisiting.

`writing-version-number` and the `version-stamp-matches-package` check are not this pack's own births either: both arrived from `cloudflare-site` (#1982) in #2101, when versioning stopped being a hosting pack's business.

### `github-pages`

The pack is genuinely new at #2101, but two of its carriers are not. The subpath rule was born in `static-website` at #611 and moved here with the serving half. The skill descends from `RELEASE.md` (#611) through `static-site-releases` (#1056), a reword at #1647, its `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` trigger at #1650, and the managed-copies rule moving out of `RULES.md` into its body at #1667, before becoming `github-pages-pipeline` at #2101. The two checks and the `site-release` task are born at #2101, the task's shape taken from `cloudflare-site`'s and its declaration rationale read off its own task README. #2182's cadence change is a `policy-changed` on the task.

### `cloudflare-site`

Born at #1982 (`Closes #1981`), generalized out of ClaudiniteWebsite's local pack, asking its adopters nothing because the published tree, the hostnames and the analytics choice are all already structural in the repo. `no-second-publisher` carries the owner's own words for why the previous host's leftovers are detected rather than listed as adoption steps. #2100 is a real `_pack` decision the brief left undrafted: the version minor gained a year offset because a bare `MMDD` runs backwards every New Year. #2101 split the versioning half out into `public-website`'s seam, leaving a delegating shim whose retirement is #2113.

### `cloudflare-workers`

One commit, 91df7ff1, landed by the `growth-discover-packs` run in #1780 (`Refs #642`). Eleven rules, each traceable to a specific artifact in `missingbulb/hitbut` or `missingbulb/WIP`'s `backend/` — that per-member mapping came off the README's evidence table and is now the per-rule `Source`. The rules had no recorded rationale beyond their own text, so their entries are short by design rather than padded. #1982 added one `_pack` entry: the routing guidance's `excludes` repointed from `static-website` to the new `cloudflare-site` sibling.

## Corrections to the brief's derivation

- **`Landed` keywords.** The brief derived `Refs #1981` for #1982 from the commit trailer; the pull request body says `Closes #1981`, and the body wins. #611 likewise carries `Closes #609`, #2182 `Closes #1995`. #2101 and #727 carry no closing keyword at all, so neither entry claims one.
- **`cloudflare-workers` was credited to a bare commit.** The brief's `Landed` read `commit 91df7ff1 (Refs #642)`. 91df7ff1 landed through #1780, which is what the unclaimed version row `60906.1` names; the entries cite the pull request, and `Actor` is the run plus who merged it.
- **#2100 read as NOTHING DRAFTED.** It touched only `bump-version.mjs`, so no carrier's text moved, but its commit body records a genuine decision about the version scheme's shape. It is now an entry on `cloudflare-site`'s `_pack`.
- **A `git log --grep` finds the wrong commit for the rules cut.** The squash commit for #2101 carries every sub-commit's message, so subject matching is useless inside it; the sub-commits were fetched by head sha (`1a410b80`) and each entry's `Model` taken from the sub-commit that actually made the change (Opus 5 for the rules cut, Fable 5.1 for the rename and the versioning move) rather than from the squash trailer's flat list.
- **The `references.md` files were read out of git before anything was truncated**, so nothing the conversion carried was dropped rather than relocated. `github-pages`' and `cloudflare-site`' deleted `references.md` were also the proof that the skill, the task and three rules never had a recorded rationale, rather than an assumption that they did.

## README and `pack.mjs` bytes

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/public-website/README.md` | 2396 | 2274 |
| `packs/public-website/pack.mjs` | 1287 | 988 |
| `packs/github-pages/README.md` | 3493 | 3088 |
| `packs/github-pages/pack.mjs` | 3272 | 2704 |
| `packs/cloudflare-site/README.md` | 3353 | 3157 |
| `packs/cloudflare-site/pack.mjs` | 4073 | 3474 |
| `packs/cloudflare-workers/README.md` | 3260 | 1758 |
| `packs/cloudflare-workers/pack.mjs` | 1304 | 1059 |

What moved: each manifest's "WHAT IS NOT HERE" and fingerprint-justification paragraphs, `public-website`'s New Year rationale for the version scheme, `github-pages`' relevance-gate and skill-triggering reasons, `cloudflare-site`'s "a checklist of no-ops teaches its reader to skim it", and `cloudflare-workers`' whole per-member evidence table — a table is history too, even though the brief's README-sections list excludes tables. `cloudflare-workers`' and `cloudflare-site`' **Upstream** reconciliation anchors stayed: that section is live state the `revalidate-from-source` task maintains, not a decision.

## Verification

- `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs check <pack>` for all four: the full file-to-carrier listing with no `(empty)` and no fault, exit 0 each.
- Full offline suite, 322 test files: **3808 tests, 3808 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: exit 0, and no finding names any of the four packs.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs`: exit 0, 0 blocking, 13 advisory — one `provenance-change-recorded` per file the `references.md` conversion had filled and this backfill rewrote. That is the case the check's own fix text sanctions ("leave it where the rewrite is the correct history (the backfill replacing what the conversion wrote) and let the diff be the record"), so it is left standing.
- `git status --porcelain` shows only `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` under the four packs. No carrier text, no check, no skill trigger and no task policy is changed; no pack version is bumped and no `VERSIONS.md` is touched.

## Predicted automerge policy

`packs/public-website/`, `packs/github-pages/`, `packs/cloudflare-site/` and `packs/cloudflare-workers/`, each limited to `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs`.

1	# claude-code-web-users-support pack
2	
3	What a project can offer the people working on it **from the web** — a Claude Code web session runs
4	for a signed-in person in a managed container, and a terminal session does neither, so this is where
5	the capabilities that depend on knowing *who* is here — or on the managed container they get —
6	live. Today that is two: the pack each person brings with them, copied into the repo by
7	[`session-prepare.mjs`](session-prepare.mjs) from a configured store repo; and
8	[`environment-setup-command.sh`](environment-setup-command.sh), the generic body a project pastes
9	into its web environment's **Setup script** field so the image carries the toolchains the base image
10	doesn't ship. The script's content is the same for every project — it just runs every active pack's
11	declared `env` install through the engine's `env-requirements.mjs`, so it never changes as
12	requirements do (bootstrap.md Part 9 walks the setup). Nobody has to go looking for that body:
13	the pack's `adoptionHandover` step has the filing session quote it inline, so the issue asking
14	for the paste carries the block to copy.
15	
16	Declared, and seeded by `--init`. The pack holds an **address**, not the content: `config.repo` (and
17	an optional `config.path`, default `preferences`) name the store that holds one `<email>/` directory
18	per person.
19	
20	## The pack a person brings
21	
22	`<path>/<email>/` in the store is an ordinary pack directory - `RULES.md`, optional `pack.mjs`,
23	`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `worldRules/`, `declared-checks.json`, `provenance/`. At session start
24	[`copy_user_pack_to_repo.mjs`](copy_user_pack_to_repo.mjs) copies it into
25	`.claudinite/temp/packs/current_user/`, the engine's session pack root, where the same loader that
26	reads the canon and the repo's own packs picks it up: its rules ride the memory channel through the
27	rules index, its skills are mounted, its checks run. So a person is not limited to stating
28	preferences - anything a pack can carry, they can carry.
29	
30	The copy runs only in an **attended** session: a routine fired under a person's account carries
31	their identity but not their presence, and the harness's attended flag is what the step reads. Every
32	miss - unattended, no identity, no configured store, no directory, a clone that fails - leaves the
33	directory holding a placeholder, and [`session-start.mjs`](session-start.mjs) turns that into one
34	plain-text note before the session proceeds on default interaction behaviour. Reading is
35	local-first: when this repo *is* the store, the working copy wins over the default branch, so an
36	edit in progress is what the session sees. Otherwise the store is reached by a shallow,
37	blob-filtered, sparse `git clone` of that one directory.
38	
39	Being the store also constrains the tree: the directory name is the whole address, so each one is
40	one person's exact identity, which [`worldRules/store-file-names.mjs`](worldRules/store-file-names.mjs)
41	explains and audits.
42	
43	**The store is as trusted as this repository.** A person's pack is executable code - checks and
44	hooks that run inside every session it is copied into - so write access to a person's directory is
45	the power to run code in their sessions. Protect the store's `<path>/` with branch protection or
46	per-directory code owners.
47	
48	What a person's pack carries is **personal, not project conventions**: conventions belong to the
49	packs that own each subject and load as prose, while these travel with a person across every project
50	they work in, and two people on one project can want different things.
51	
52	## Rules (`RULES.md`)
53	
54	| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
55	|---|---|---|---|
56	| Changing a person's rules | medium | complexity | prose: <100 words |
57	| A person's first personal pack | high | correctness | prose: <50 words + check (`preferences-store-file-names`) |
58	| A person wanting more than rules | medium | complexity | prose: <100 words |
59	| A web session's missing toolchain | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
60	
61	## Checks
62	
63	All three are advisory: a personal pack is a nice-to-have, and nothing here may block a session.
64	
65	| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
66	|---|---|---|---|
67	| `preferences-store-configured` | medium | complexity | check: advisory |
68	| `preferences-store-file-names` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
69	| `preferences-provenance` | low | complexity | check: advisory |

input.title: Provenance: correct four _pack files that cite Refs where the PR closed its issue
input.head: claude/correct-landed-closes-refs
input.body:
Corrects a defect in #2213, which is merged. Advances #2169; closes nothing.

## The defect

Eleven `Landed` lines across four `_pack.md` files cite `Refs` where the pull request's body closed its issue:

| Pack | Entries | Trailer says | Body says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `android`, `app-store-release`, `play-store-release` | #165 | `Refs #180` | `Closes #180` |
| same three | #1634 | `Refs #1632` | `Closes #1632` |
| same three | #1667 | `Refs #1662` | `Closes #1662` |
| `html` | #128 | `Refs #127, #131` | `Closes #127` / `Closes #131` |
| `html` | #1634 | `Refs #1632` | `Closes #1632` |

`Closes` is what fills GitHub's Development panel and resolves the issue. `Refs` is a bare cross-reference and links nothing there, so the entries send a reader tracing which issue this pack's work closed to the wrong kind of link.

The cause is that `provenance.mjs brief` derives `Landed` from the **commit trailer**, and on these older pull requests the trailer and the body disagree. Three independent runs of the backfill since have now found the same disagreement on every older pull request they checked — eighteen occurrences across ten packs. The trailer is not a shortcut to the body; it is a wrong answer more often than not.

## The fix
